Inclusion criteria met: none clearly satisfied. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not task-based), I2 (no emotion regulation task/strategy reported), I4 (no task-related activation results), I3 not demonstrated (clinical sample implied but control group not reported).

Task-based fMRI study in healthy human participants viewing emotional visual stimuli; examines habitual emotion regulation (expressive suppression), including anticipatory/antecedent processes, and reports task-related brain activation. No exclusion criteria met. Abstract does not clearly state instructed regulation, so full-text review is warranted to confirm details.

Study addresses emotion circuitry and regulation in human first-degree relatives but abstract does not specify whether a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation (view vs regulate) paradigm was used or whether task-related activation results are reported. Insufficient information to confirm I1, I2, and I4, but I3 (human participants) is met. Include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in adult humans using instructed cognitive reappraisal (Social-Reg) versus look, reporting task-related brain activation contrasts and associations with behavior; meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are evident.

Task-based fMRI study of human participants using cognitive reappraisal to regulate emotion; reports task-related brain activation (PFC) and includes younger and older groups. Satisfies I1–I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract does not report whether this is a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study or whether task-related activation contrasts meet inclusion criteria. Title suggests affect processing in methamphetamine dependence but provides insufficient detail. Include for full-text review to determine I1, I2, and I4.

No evidence this is a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation. The abstract describes altered structural/white-matter connectivity in GAD (likely DTI), not an emotion-regulation task or task-related activation. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation); I3 (human participants) is implied but control group not specified.

Task-based fMRI where participants ignored task-irrelevant unpleasant words (emotional interference), representing cognitive control of emotion/emotion regulation; includes non-patient groups (high AP/AR/AD and controls) and reports task-related functional connectivity results. All inclusion criteria I1–I4 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI retinotopic mapping), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain mapping results). Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (no emotion regulation task—participants did not regulate emotional responses; study focused on visual field mapping and resting-state connectivity). No evidence of emotion regulation or related task activations; therefore excluded.

Abstract examines neural correlates of emotion regulation in late-life GAD (human clinical sample). However, it does not specify use of a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm nor clearly report task-related activation in the abstract. Insufficient information to confirm I1 and I4, so include for full-text review.

No task-based emotion regulation paradigm reported: study uses resting-state fMRI examining inflammation and rsFC. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants implied). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation task), I4 (no task-related activation reported).

Task-based fMRI with human participants; task involves active vs passive maintenance of emotional responses (an emotion-regulation-like strategy), and the abstract reports task-related brain activation results. Fits broad definition of emotion regulation in I2. No exclusion criteria met.

No task-based fMRI or task-related activation reported: the study used resting-state fMRI and measured spontaneous (trait) reappraisal. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion-regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results). Exclusion criteria met: none.

Excluded: Study uses resting-state fMRI (no task); does not involve an emotion-regulation or viewing task and does not report task-related activation. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study where MDD participants performed a voluntary emotion regulation strategy (recalling negative autobiographical memories) with BOLD contrasts reported; includes clinical and control groups. No exclusion criteria met. Full text warranted to confirm stimulus modality relative to review objective.

Study is a structural VBM MRI study (not task-based fMRI), does not involve an emotion-regulation task, and does not report task-related brain activation results. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3. Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1, I2, I4.

E2: Study examines neural responses/empathy to infant cries without instructions to amplify or dampen emotions (no emotion regulation task). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human fathers), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no emotion-regulation instructions or task).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of female adolescents with conduct disorder performing effortful emotion regulation and reports dorsolateral prefrontal activation differences (task-related activation). The abstract does not clearly state whether a separate control group is included. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract lacks sufficient detail to confirm I1 (task-based fMRI) and I2 (participants instructed to regulate emotion) or whether visual emotional stimuli were merely viewed; title suggests negative emotional distraction but task details and presence of control group are not reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Task-based fMRI in human clinical and control groups reporting task-related ACC activations during an emotionally salient cue-reactivity task. The abstract does not state explicit emotion-regulation instructions, but the meta-analysis objective allows viewing without regulating; full text needed to confirm whether an explicit regulation contrast exists. Include for full-text review.

Excluded because E2 applies: this is an empathy/perspective-taking task (MET) with no evidence participants were instructed to amplify or dampen their emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical + control groups), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (no demonstrated emotion regulation instructions).

This study reports associations between subclinical symptoms and brain structure in a non-clinical sample (structural imaging), not a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human healthy participants). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in depressed adolescents, reporting task-related brain activation differences; meets inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI, emotion regulation (reappraisal), applicable participant groups (clinical adolescents with control comparison), and reports activation results. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes task-based fMRI with human participants and task-related activations, but does not involve an emotion-regulation instruction or strategy (e.g., reappraisal/acceptance) nor explicit regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli; therefore I2 not met. No exclusion criteria clearly apply.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of volitional regulation of desire for food (an emotion/craving regulation task) in human participants and examines hemodynamic responses (brain activation). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text should be reviewed to confirm stimulus modality (likely visual) and task details.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria: I3 met (human trauma-exposed healthy participants with controls). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I1 (study is structural and functional-connectivity, not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion-regulation task described), I4 (no task-related activation results reported). Excluded for not meeting task-based/emotion-regulation fMRI criteria.

Exclude because imaging modality is MEG, not task-based fMRI (I1 not met). Abstract does meet I2 (emotion regulation via cognitive reappraisal), I3 (human participants), and I4 (reports task-related neural activation/oscillatory power). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) are met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study where human participants (MDD patients and healthy controls) performed an instructed emotion-regulation task (internal/external causal attributions) while viewing emotional faces, and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results. This meets inclusion criteria I1–I4 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

No task-based fMRI or emotion regulation task reported. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). The study reports resting cerebral blood flow and HF-HRV correlations, not task-related fMRI activation during emotion regulation.

Task-based fMRI study of human participants performing cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation). Abstract reports task-related brain activation results (amygdala, prefrontal) during regulation. No exclusion criteria met.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment in humans that reports task-related brain activation (I1, I3, I4 satisfied). However, the abstract does not clearly state that participants were instructed to perform an emotion regulation task (I2 is uncertain)—while acceptance of unfair offers is discussed as involving regulatory processes, explicit regulation instructions are not described. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to determine I2.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in interpersonal trauma survivors with PTSD and healthy controls, reporting relationships between affect and regional brain activation. Inclusion is uncertain regarding whether the task involves explicit emotion regulation versus passive/non-conscious emotional viewing and whether stimuli were visual; therefore include for full-text review.

Abstract reports an fMRI study in bipolar disorder (human clinical sample) examining cortico-amygdala circuit dysfunction, but does not specify a task-based emotion-regulation or viewing paradigm or report task-related activation. Insufficient information to determine I1, I2, and I4 from the abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

This is a task-based fMRI study reporting BOLD responses in phobic participants viewing phobia-related images, but the abstract does not describe any emotion-regulation instructions or strategies (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance). Inclusion criterion I2 (emotion regulation task) is not met, so the study is excluded.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants - healthy humans). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). The study reports structural gray-matter volume differences related to a genetic polymorphism, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation experiment.

Meets inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in human participants (children/adolescents with ASD and TD controls) and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results. No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI (I1) with clinical and control groups (I3) and task-related activation reported (I4). The abstract describes passive viewing of fearful/neutral faces but provides no evidence participants were instructed to regulate emotion (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria met; include for full-text review.

Study examines emotion recognition (viewing/perception) in MDD rather than an emotion regulation task. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based functional imaging) and I4 (reports task-related functional alterations). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no evidence participants were instructed to regulate/dampen/amplify emotional responses), I3 (patient/control group reporting not clearly stated). No exclusion criteria met.

fMRI study with task-based functional analyses of perceptual processing of fearful visual stimuli in healthy humans, reporting task-related activation and coupling. The abstract does not describe an emotion-regulation instruction (uncertain if passive viewing is eligible under review scope), so include for full-text review to determine whether it meets the regulation/viewing criteria.

This is a resting-state fMRI study of inflammation-induced anxiety, not a task-based emotion regulation or viewing task. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion NOT met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results). No exclusion criteria met.

No evidence the task involved emotion regulation of visual stimuli. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical groups reported), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I2 (emotion regulation task such as reappraisal) — study investigates reward processing (monetary) rather than regulating emotional responses to visual stimuli.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion I3 met (human postpartum participants). Inclusion I1 not met (resting-state, not task-based fMRI), I2 not met (no emotion regulation task; resting connectivity only), I4 not met (reports resting-state connectivity, not task-related activation). Therefore excluded for not meeting core task-based emotion-regulation study criteria.

Task-based fMRI with 20 healthy human participants viewing aversive visual stimuli and reporting task-related BOLD activation. Abstract does not describe an instructed emotion-regulation task, but the review objective includes passive viewing of emotional stimuli; thus study is eligible for full-text review.

Abstract reports a human study of cognitive reappraisal of negative self-beliefs in social anxiety disorder and addresses neural mechanisms, meeting emotion-regulation task relevance. However, the abstract does not explicitly state that task-based fMRI was used or that visual stimuli were presented, so inclusion on abstract alone is uncertain — full text needed to confirm I1 and I4 (and whether controls reported for I3).

Does not address review objective of regulating emotional responses to visual stimuli: task uses recall of autobiographical memories (non-visual). No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based rtfMRI neurofeedback), I2 (emotion regulation task via upregulation), I3 (human clinical and control groups). Inclusion criterion not demonstrated: I4 (task-related brain activation results not clearly reported).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of human participants using voluntary suppression of negative affect (an emotion regulation strategy) and examining neural substrates, reporting task-related brain activation results. This meets I1–I4 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

No exclusion criteria met. Human participants are included (I3 met). Not a task-based fMRI activation study—uses resting-state functional connectivity after script-driven imagery (I1 not met). No explicit emotion-regulation task described (I2 not met). Does not report task-related activation results (I4 not met).

Abstract reports human PTSD and control groups and examines directed connectivity in emotion/fear circuitry, but does not explicitly state a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm or report task-related activation. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to determine whether I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), and I4 (task-related activation results) are satisfied.

Excluded: study is structural VBM correlational MRI using a questionnaire of habitual expressive suppression, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation experiment. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of human participants performing cognitive reappraisal (down-/up-regulation) of visual/episodic negative images, reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria met.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none (no evidence in abstract). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (study is resting-state fMRI, not task-based), I2 (does not involve an emotion regulation task or viewing/regulating emotional visual stimuli), I4 (no task-related activation reported). I3 (participant type not clearly demonstrated in abstract). Therefore excluded.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (downregulation, upregulation, passive viewing) in human participants and reports task-related brain activation differences by genotype; no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a human task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (distancing) to regulate negative emotions, includes adult participants, and reports task-related neural results (amygdala–prefrontal connectivity and amygdala activity over time). No exclusion criteria are met from the abstract.

Task-based fMRI with human participants viewing emotionally salient child videos; reports task-related brain activation. Abstract does not state explicit emotion-regulation instructions, but the review includes studies that merely view visual emotional stimuli without regulating, so inclusion is uncertain from abstract alone — include for full-text review.

No explicit emotion-regulation instructions or strategy are described; the study examines anticipatory neural activity during speech anticipation but not a regulation task. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I2. Exclusion criteria met: none (E1/E2 not applicable).

Excluded because the study is not a task-based fMRI study (it uses EEG effective-connectivity), so I1 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain/connectivity results). No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation (self-distraction/thought suppression) in an anticipatory anxiety paradigm, reporting neural activation results in humans. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a resting-state fMRI study (no task). The abstract does not describe a task-based emotion regulation or viewing task, nor task-related activation results. Exclusion criteria: none met. Inclusion criteria met: none demonstrated. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation/viewing task), I4 (task-related brain activation results); I3 (participant/control group) not demonstrated in abstract.

This is a task-based fMRI study where participants viewed affective visual stimuli and the paper reports task-related brain activation and individual-difference correlations. It meets I1, I3, and I4. The abstract does not describe an explicit emotion-regulation instruction (I2 not demonstrated), but the review objective includes passive viewing studies; thus include for full-text review to confirm eligibility.

Not a task-based emotion regulation fMRI study. The study reports structural (cortical thickness) and functional connectivity analyses based on expressive suppression trait measures, without any task or task-related activation results, so it does not meet task-based or task-activation criteria.

No emotion regulation task is described and stimuli are auditory (music/nonmusical sounds) rather than visual, so the study does not match the review objective. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I2 (no evidence of an emotion regulation task); I4 (task-related activation results not clearly reported in abstract).

Study uses resting-state fMRI (connectivity) rather than a task-based emotion-regulation or viewing task. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion-regulation task), I4 (task-related activation).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion NOT met or not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; resting-state), I2 (no emotion regulation task), I4 (does not report task-related activation; reports resting-state connectivity).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of attention network dysfunction in bulimia nervosa, not an emotion-regulation task. Inclusion I1, I3, and I4 appear met; I2 (emotion regulation task/viewing emotional stimuli with/without regulation) is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria from E1–E2 apply.

Task-based rtfMRI neurofeedback study in humans training down-regulation of amygdala during presentation of negative emotional faces using a regulation strategy ('reality checking'); reports task-related amygdala activation changes and compares to passive viewing; healthy participants. Meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in human young adults and task-related brain activation (I1, I3, I4). However, it does not state participants were instructed to regulate their emotions or perform an emotion-regulation strategy (I2 not demonstrated). Inclusion for full-text review is warranted to determine whether an emotion-regulation component was present.

Abstract reports a randomized, placebo-controlled task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in healthy adults and presents task-related activation and functional connectivity results (amygdala and dlPFC). No exclusion criteria are met from the abstract. Full-text review warranted to extract details.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of human participants performing cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation), includes adolescent/young adult sample, and reports task-related brain activation results (amygdala and PFC). No exclusion criteria met.
Resting-state fMRI study with no task or emotion-regulation instructions; reports connectivity, not task-related activations. Exclude because it does not meet task-based/emotion-regulation criteria.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal strategy (core emotion-regulation approach) with reported neural activity/connectivity and refers to human participants. It does not specify regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli explicitly, so inclusion in the visual-stimulus-specific meta-analysis is uncertain — include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI in healthy humans (n=18) using an emotion regulation task (reappraisal) and reporting task-related activations (vmPFC, amygdala). Abstract does not specify whether emotional stimuli were visual, so insufficient information to confirm the review's visual-stimulus requirement; include for full-text review to determine stimulus modality. No exclusion criteria met.

E2: The study is an fMRI moral-decision and perspective-taking experiment where participants were humanized via implicit mentalizing primes but were not instructed to amplify or dampen their emotional responses (no emotion-regulation instructions). Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion not met: I2 (emotion regulation task not demonstrated).

E2: Study examines perception/evaluation of others (active listening) without instructions to amplify or dampen participants' own emotional responses (no emotion-regulation instruction). Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion not met: I2 (no evidence of an emotion-regulation task such as reappraisal or instructed modulation).

Study used auditory emotional stimuli (sounds), not visual stimuli, so it does not address the review objective. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I2 (uncertain whether compassion meditation here counts as an emotion regulation task).

Task-based fMRI study in humans where participants were instructed to up- and down-regulate emotional responses to aversive visual scenes (cognitive reappraisal strategies), and the abstract reports task-related brain activation results (prefrontal, amygdala). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI in human participants using distancing (a form of cognitive reappraisal) to downregulate emotional responses to visual social stimuli; reports whole-brain task-related activation results (amygdala, PFC, precuneus, etc.). Meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apparent.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of voluntary emotion regulation that reduces amygdala activation to aversive stimuli, indicating human participants performed an emotion regulation task and task-related brain activation was reported. No exclusion criteria are met from the abstract.

E2 met: participants judged another's affect (perspective-taking/empathy) with no instruction to amplify/dampen their own emotions. Inclusion: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human older adult sample), I4 (reports task-related brain activation) are satisfied. Inclusion I2 is not demonstrated (no emotion-regulation instructions reported).

Abstract describes human clinical groups (MDD with/without comorbid anxiety) and neural engagement of cognitive control and subgenual cingulate, suggesting task-related brain activation; however it does not explicitly state use of task-based fMRI or that participants performed an emotion regulation task. Insufficient information to confirm I1, I2, and I4 — include for full-text review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study assessing the influence of induced emotions on a cognitive task, indicating I1 and I4 are met. It does not specify that participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 not demonstrated). Insufficient detail to determine regulation task presence, so include for full-text review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study (I1) where participants explicitly regulate emotion (reduce negative, enhance positive) reflecting CBT-like reappraisal strategies (I2), includes human clinical (medication-free MDD) and matched control groups reported separately (I3), and reports task-related brain activation results (I4). No exclusion criteria are met.

Resting-state fMRI study with no task-based emotion regulation; reports associations between spontaneous activity and resilience/well-being rather than task-related activation. No exclusion criteria met.

No task-based fMRI: this is a resting-state connectivity study, not a task where participants regulate or view emotional stimuli. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical and control groups reported). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results).

Abstract reports investigation of emotional reactivity and cognitive regulation during social and physical threat in social anxiety disorder (human participants), indicating an emotion-regulation task but does not explicitly state task-based fMRI or report task-related activation in the abstract. Inclusion is uncertain from abstract-only evidence, so include for full-text review.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (not an emotion regulation task; study reports appetitive conditioning without instructions to regulate emotional responses). The abstract does not describe any reappraisal/acceptance/distancing or other regulation instructions, so it does not meet the review objective.

Study used resting-state (not task-based) fMRI and did not report an emotion-regulation task or task-related activations. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical participants with TBI). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results).

Exclusion: No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2). Inclusion: Human participants present (I3 met). Not eligible because it is not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met), does not involve an emotion-regulation task (I2 not met), and does not report task-related brain activation results (I4 not met). This is a DTI structural connectivity study predicting trait anxiety, outside the review's fMRI emotion-regulation scope.

Task-based human fMRI study where smokers viewed emotionally evocative anti-smoking messages; reports task-related activations (amygdala, vmPFC) and a regulation-related brain pattern moderating responses. Fits I1 (task fMRI), I2 (viewing/regulating emotional stimuli), I3 (human participants), and I4 (task-related activation results). No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI study reporting task-related cortical–amygdala coupling during anticipation of a public speech (I1, I4). It examines anticipatory emotional processes relevant to emotion regulation, but the abstract does not state that participants were instructed to regulate nor whether a control group is reported, so full-text review is needed to confirm I2 and I3.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I3 (human adolescent sample). Inclusion NOT met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task during scanning), I4 (task-related brain activation results). Study reports structural MRI and questionnaires only.

Task-based fMRI in human participants directly comparing multiple emotion regulation strategies (detachment, reinterpretation, distraction, expressive suppression) during downregulation of negative emotions; reports task-related brain activation (prefrontal, amygdala) fitting the meta-analysis objective. No exclusion criteria evident.

Abstract does not report whether task-based fMRI or an emotion regulation task was used; it describes machine-learning on multimodal neuroimaging in PTSD (human clinical sample). I3 appears met, but I1, I2, and I4 are not demonstrated in the abstract. Include for full-text review to determine task nature and task-related activation reporting.

Abstract reports neural and behavioural responses during anticipatory fear in men with schizophrenia or APD (human clinical sample), but does not explicitly state task-based fMRI, an emotion-regulation instruction, or task-related activation results. I3 is clearly met; I1, I2, and I4 are not demonstrated in the abstract. Include for full-text review to confirm imaging and task details.

Abstract reports a human trial teaching cognitive reappraisal to alter neural (reward/inhibitory region) responses to high-fat/high-sugar foods, meeting I2 (emotion regulation/cognitive reappraisal) and I3 (human participants). The abstract does not explicitly state task-based fMRI (I1) or clearly report task-related brain activation results (I4), so full-text review is needed to confirm fMRI and activation reporting.

Task-based fMRI study reporting cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal) during scanning in human participants (female sample) with task-related brain activation results (amygdala and prefrontal coupling). No exclusion criteria met and all inclusion criteria are satisfied.

Exclusion based on study using voxel-based structural MRI (VBM) rather than task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigms. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). No exclusion criteria from E1–E2 apply.

This is an fMRI study using a re-appraisal emotion regulation task in human participants (cocaine-dependent and matched controls) and reports task-related activations and connectivity, meeting all inclusion criteria.

Task-based fMRI study using a Stroop Match-to-Sample with emotional (angry face) interference; examines prefrontal cognitive control over emotion and reports task-related activations and functional connectivity in adolescents with Internet gaming disorder and controls. Meets inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI, cognitive control of emotion, eligible participant groups, and reporting task-related brain activation. No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Abstract reports human older adult clinical and control groups with neuroimaging of PFC activity/connectivity (meets I3). However, it does not specify a task-based fMRI paradigm, nor that participants performed an emotion-regulation task or that task-related activation results are reported (I1, I2, I4 not demonstrated). Insufficient information to determine inclusion—include for full-text review.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in 9–19-year-olds and task-related amygdala activation (I1, I3, I4 met). However, it does not describe an emotion regulation instruction or strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other regulation), so I2 is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria (E1, E2) are met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans using an emotion regulation (reappraisal/maintain/suppress) task, includes clinical (cocaine+Cluster B) and control groups, and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results. Satisfies inclusion criteria; no exclusion criteria apparent from abstract.

Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants: African American youths followed into adulthood). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation). Study reports resting-state functional connectivity, not a task-based emotion regulation fMRI study.

Abstract provides insufficient information to determine whether participants performed an emotion-regulation task or whether a control group and task-based activations are reported. It is clearly a task-based fMRI study (I1), but I2, I3, and I4 are not demonstrated—include for full-text review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI RCT where patients viewed negative images or intentionally down-regulated affect using taught strategies, reports symptom change and normalization of brain activation—meeting all inclusion criteria and no exclusions evident.

The study reports a task-based fMRI emotional face processing task in healthy adults and presents task-related activation/connectivity results (I1, I3, I4). The abstract does not specify an emotion-regulation instruction (I2 is unclear), but the review accepts studies that view emotional stimuli without regulating; therefore include for full-text review to resolve this. No exclusion criteria met.

Study is a task-based fMRI with human participants instructed to maintain or regulate emotional responses to visual social stimuli (regulation task). Reports task-related brain activation analyses. No exclusion criteria met (not a review; not mere perspective-taking).

Study uses resting-state fMRI rather than a task-based emotion regulation or viewing paradigm. It includes clinical (ASD) and control participants (I3 met) but does not involve an emotion regulation task (I2), is not task-based (I1), and does not report task-related activation results (I4). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

Resting-state fMRI twin study; not task-based and does not involve an emotion regulation task or report task-related activations. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation).

Excluded because the study does not involve an emotion regulation task as defined (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (no emotion regulation instruction; study examines price-driven expectations on taste, not deliberate regulation of emotional responses). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply based on the abstract.

No task-based fMRI or task-related activation reported. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical sample with control group). Inclusion NOT met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). Exclusion criteria met: none.

Task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotions; human participants including an anxiety-prone group and healthy controls; reports task-related BOLD activation contrasts during regulation versus maintain. Meets inclusion criteria I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study where human participants used cognitive reappraisal to up- and downregulate emotional responses to visual threat-related stimuli; reports task-related brain activation (amygdala, prefrontal regions) and physiological/self-report measures. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract does not specify a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm or report task-related activation results; it discusses neural indicators of anger and stress symptoms in (presumably) human participants. Key inclusion criteria (I1, I2, I4) are not demonstrated in the abstract, so full-text review is needed to determine eligibility.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI, uses distraction as an emotion regulation strategy, involves human clinical and control groups, and reports task-related neural activation results. No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to extract detailed ROI/contrast data.

Abstract reports an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy men and women using emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal and distraction) and presents task-related brain activation results; no exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI with human participants and task-related activation reported (I1, I3, I4). Abstract does not indicate an explicit emotion-regulation instruction or strategy (I2 unclear); study examines individual differences in external motivation during face evaluation. No exclusion criteria clearly met. Include for full-text review to determine whether an emotion-regulation task was used.

Participants were passively exposed to infant cry sounds; no emotion regulation instructions or task are described (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activation). Exclusion criteria met: none (E1,E2 not applicable).

Task-based fMRI with human participants reporting task-related brain activation during Ultimatum Game decisions. The study involves acceptance (an allowed regulation-like strategy), but the abstract does not state explicit emotion-regulation instructions; include for full-text review to confirm I2.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of neural responses to frustration in children, but does not specify an emotion-regulation instruction, whether stimuli were visual, whether a control group is reported, or provide task activation details. Insufficient information to confirm I2, I3, and I4, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal to regulate negative emotions and reporting neuronal correlates in borderline patients. Abstract does not clearly state whether a separate control group is reported, so full text needed to confirm I3. Include for full-text review.

The study is a task-based fMRI study (I1), with human participants (I3), and reports task-related activations (I4), but it does not involve participants performing an emotion regulation task—it uses an emotional oddball/distraction paradigm without instructions to regulate emotional responses (I2 not met). No exclusion criteria are met (none applicable).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation reported). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I2 — not an emotion-regulation task and stimuli are auditory (infant laughter), whereas the meta-analysis targets regulation or passive viewing of visual stimuli. Thus study does not address the review objective.

Task-based fMRI with human participants and reports task-related brain activation, but abstract does not clearly state participants were instructed to perform an emotion regulation task. No exclusion criteria clearly met; insufficient information on I2, so include for full-text review.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants including clinical and control groups), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion I2 NOT met: the task involved implicit processing/viewing of emotional faces without instructions to regulate emotion (no reappraisal/other regulation strategy reported).

Abstract suggests neural investigation of regulating negative autobiographical memories but does not clearly state task-based fMRI, that participants performed an explicit emotion-regulation task, or that task-related activation results are reported. Insufficient information to confirm inclusion criteria from abstract alone; include for full-text review.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adolescents reporting task-related brain activations. However, the abstract does not clearly state that participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (it examines emotional interference, not explicit regulation). I2 is therefore unclear from the abstract; include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Abstract reports a fear-conditioning/generalization fMRI task without any instruction to regulate emotional responses. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion ID not met: I2 (no emotion-regulation task reported).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans (N=20) with task-related brain activation and healthy participants. It is unclear whether participants were instructed to regulate emotions (vs. passive viewing); therefore inclusion for full-text review is warranted to determine if the task meets the review's emotion-regulation criteria.

Abstract lacks methodological detail: it does not state whether fMRI was task-based, whether participants performed an emotion-regulation task, or whether task-related activation results are reported. The study appears to involve human participants exposed to early life stress, so I3 is met. Because key inclusion criteria (I1, I2, I4) are not demonstrated from the abstract, include for full-text review.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I2 (participants performing an emotion-regulation task as defined) — the study manipulates pain/anxiety via behavioral control and safety cues but does not report instructed emotion-regulation (e.g., reappraisal) of visual stimuli. Therefore exclude based on I2 not being satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI study with human participants that reports task-related activations (I1, I3, I4). However, participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses; the manipulation was social sharing vs. alone (no reappraisal/other regulation), so I2 is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports fMRI measures of affective processing when participants evaluated affective stimuli, compares meditation versus active control, and reports task-related connectivity and dynamic causal modeling linking brain changes to affective processing. Human elderly participants were used. These elements meet the review’s task-based fMRI and emotion-processing criteria, though the abstract is slightly ambiguous about explicit regulation instructions; inclusion errs toward full-text review.

Abstract reports an fMRI study of older adults with amnestic MCI addressing affective regulation and frontal dysfunction, but does not specify a task-based emotion regulation paradigm or task-related activation results. Insufficient detail to confirm I1, I2, and I4 from the abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Abstract describes passive processing of emotional words in a task-based fMRI study with healthy participants and reports task-related activation and connectivity. However, it does not report an instructed emotion-regulation task (only mentions possible 'unintentional' regulation). Therefore I2 (emotion regulation task) is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract does not show participants performed an emotion-regulation task (I2). It reports reappraisal of meaning for literary texts but not instruction to regulate emotional responses to stimuli; stimuli are textual rather than clearly emotional visual images. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I2. No exclusion criteria clearly met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of cognitive emotion regulation in previously depressed and healthy children, reporting neural activation differences during regulation. Meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, and I4; no exclusion criteria evident.

This is a resting-state fMRI study that did not use a task or an emotion-regulation paradigm, and it does not report task-related activation. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion-regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results). Exclusion criteria met: none.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I1 (task-based fMRI: scanned retrieval session with neural recruitment), I3 (human participants across ages), I4 (reports task-related brain activation/connectivity). Not satisfied: I2 — participants performed memory retrieval and vividness ratings but were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses; no emotion-regulation task is described in the abstract.

Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants across ages including adolescents), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (no evidence participants performed an emotion-regulation task; they viewed social cues and performed a cognitive control task but were not instructed to regulate emotions).

Abstract implies brain imaging with reported activation of emotion-regulation neurocircuits but does not specify whether participants performed an emotion regulation task or whether humans were tested. Insufficient information to confirm all inclusion criteria, so include for full-text review.

Study used voxel-based morphometry (structural MRI) correlating gray matter density with task performance rather than task-based fMRI activation. Thus it does not meet I1 (task-based fMRI) nor I4 (reports task-related activation). It does include an emotional conflict resolution task (I2) in adults (I3).

Study is a task-based fMRI investigation in human juvenile schizophrenia patients with reported task-related activations (I1, I3, I4 met). However, it uses an emotion discrimination/viewing task without any instruction to regulate or modulate emotional responses, so I2 (emotion regulation task) is not met. No exclusion criteria apply (none met).

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of children using cognitive reappraisal to regulate emotional responses to visual (sad) stimuli, and reports task-related brain activation (PFC, amygdala). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation instruction). Recommend full-text review.

EXCLUDED because the study does not address emotion regulation of visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (emotion regulation task) — study examines intrinsic motivation and responses to errors/reward, not regulation of emotional responses. No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

Excluded because the abstract reports a task-based fMRI cue-exposure study with alcoholic and social drinker groups and task-related activations (meets I1, I3, I4) but does not describe any emotion-regulation instructions (reappraisal, distancing, regulation during anticipation/cue) and appears to be passive cue-reactivity; therefore I2 is not met. No exclusion criteria are met (none).

Abstract is truncated and provides insufficient information to determine whether participants performed an emotion-regulation task (I2). Title indicates a human task-based fMRI fear-conditioning study reporting BOLD results in vmPFC, satisfying I1, I3, and I4. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to assess whether emotion regulation instructions were used.

Abstract reports human participants and neural activation in a task paradigm but does not clearly state use of fMRI (I1) or that the task is an emotion-regulation instruction (I2). Insufficient information to confirm these inclusion criteria; full-text review needed to verify imaging modality and whether the task fits the review’s definition of regulation.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in human adolescents/young adults that reports task-related brain activation results (meets I1–I4). No exclusion criteria apply. Abstract provides sufficient info to include for full-text review.

E2 met: study is a mentalizing/Prisoner's Dilemma fMRI task without instruction to amplify or dampen participants' own emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (not an emotion-regulation task).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in adolescent girls with PTSD and reports task-related amygdala functional connectivity changes associated with symptom reduction. This meets inclusion criteria I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria are indicated in the abstract.

Abstract describes an empirical task-based fMRI study in humans using cognitive reappraisal to regulate emotion, reports task-related brain activation results, and includes clinical and control groups. No exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract reports investigation of neural activity during cognitive reappraisal using simultaneous EEG-fMRI, indicating an emotion-regulation task and task-based fMRI; however it does not specify visual stimuli or clearly state task-related activation results, so include for full-text review to confirm eligibility.

Task-based fMRI with human participants (N=10) performing emotion regulation tasks (reappraisal and affect labeling) and reporting task-related brain activation (amygdala, IFG). Tasks involve regulating emotional responses and fit the meta-analysis objective. No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded because the study examines regulation of pain (somatosensory) rather than regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli required by the review objective. Abstract meets I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation/anticipation/acceptance), I3 (human participants), and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) apply. However, it does not address emotional regulation of visual stimuli, so it falls outside the meta-analysis objective.

Task-based fMRI study in human participants using cognitive reappraisal (an emotion regulation task) that reports task-related neural activation results and comparisons. No exclusion criteria apparent. Abstract satisfies inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, and I4.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (participants did not perform an emotion-regulation task or were not instructed to regulate). Also study used auditory comments, not visual stimuli required by the review objective, so it does not address the review question.

Abstract does not explicitly state task-based fMRI or that participants were instructed to regulate emotions, but it investigates neurobiological mechanisms of a positivity bias in older adults and reports anterior cingulate activation, indicating human participants and brain activation. Exclusion criteria not met. Insufficient information to confirm I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), and I4 (task-related activation reported) from abstract alone — include for full-text review.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans using emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and distraction) with remitted depressed patients and healthy controls, and reports task-related brain activation (amygdala, ACC, OFC). Meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are indicated.

Task-based fMRI study (I1) with children and adults viewing emotional video clips and reporting task-related brain activation results (I4). Participant sample qualifies (I3). The abstract does not state an explicit emotion-regulation instruction (I2 not demonstrated), but the review objective allows passive viewing; include for full-text review to confirm applicability.

This is a resting-state fMRI connectivity study in veterans with/without PTSD, not a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation).

EXCLUDED: No task-based emotion-regulation paradigm reported — study used resting-state fMRI of habitual reappraisal and RSFC. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion-regulation task during scanning), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results). Exclusion criteria met: none.

Task-based fMRI study using an antecedent-focused, extrinsic/incidental reappraisal strategy (precedent descriptions) in human participants; reports modulation of amygdala and insula responses (task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met based on abstract. Full text recommended for extraction of details.

EXCLUDED because the study is structural morphometry (sulcal variability/volumetry) in healthy participants, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human healthy participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I1 (task-based event-related fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I2 (this study manipulated attention to emotional stimuli via rTMS and cueing but did not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses).

Task-based fMRI study examining neural circuitry supporting emotion regulation using an emotional n-back task in human clinical groups; reports task-related anterior cingulate activation distinguishing bipolar vs unipolar depressed females. Inclusion criteria I1, I3, and I4 are clearly met; I2 is reasonably met because the study targets emotion regulation circuitry and uses emotional stimuli (fits the review objective of regulation or viewing). No exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI in humans reporting task-related activations (I1, I3, I4). Abstract does not clearly indicate an instructed emotion-regulation task or that participants performed regulation of visual stimuli (I2 not demonstrated); insufficient information to determine inclusion, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study of implicit emotion processing (gender discrimination) in healthy human participants that reports task-related activation (amygdala BOLD response and functional connectivity) to emotional facial expressions. Although not an explicit regulation task, the meta-analysis includes passive viewing of emotional stimuli, so inclusion criterion for emotion-regulation/viewing is satisfied.

Meets key inclusion criteria: task-based functional MRI (arterial spin-labeling) with an explicit emotion regulation task (worry induction and reappraisal), human clinical and control groups, and task-related activation results reported. Abstract does not specify visual stimuli (uses personalized worry scripts) and modality details could affect eligibility for the review; therefore include for full-text review to resolve stimulus modality and confirm fMRI compatibility.

No evidence of an emotion regulation instruction (I2 not met). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants; control group reported), I4 (task-related brain activation results). Inclusion not met: I2 (study used incidental emotional processing during a gender-discrimination task; participants were not instructed to regulate emotion). No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2).

Study uses resting-state fMRI and baseline HRV rather than a task-based emotion regulation paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human adult participants across ages). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a well-validated emotion regulation task in human participants (drug-naïve IGD youth and matched controls) and presents task-related brain activation results, satisfying inclusion criteria I1–I4. No exclusion criteria are met.

Study used resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) rather than a task-based paradigm. It does not involve an emotion-regulation task with visual stimuli or report task-related activation results. It includes human clinical participants (MDD) but fails I1, I2, and I4. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a resting-state fMRI study of adolescent girls (no task or emotion-regulation paradigm). It therefore does not meet I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), or I4 (task-related activation results). I3 (human adolescent participants) is met. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

Task-based fMRI with human participants performing an emotion regulation task (up-regulation of positive emotions to visual images), healthy sample, and reports task-related brain activation (ventral striatum). No exclusion criteria met in abstract.

Abstract indicates clinical human participants (catatonia) and reports orbitofrontal signal changes during emotional processing, suggesting task-related brain activation results. However it does not specify task-based fMRI methods or that participants performed an emotion regulation or viewing task. Insufficient detail to confirm I1 or I2, so include for full-text review.

No exclusion criteria met (E1/E2: none). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met / not demonstrated: I2 — the study examines pain processing/meditation during thermal stimulation, not regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli as specified by the review objective. Therefore excluded for not addressing the review objective.

This is a resting-state fMRI study of emotional intelligence, not a task-based emotion regulation study. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results). No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2 not applicable).

Exclusion: None (no exclusion criteria met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (no emotion regulation instruction—passive viewing of emotional faces). The study does not involve an instructed emotion-regulation task, so it is excluded.

Task-based fMRI study using attentional distraction as an emotion regulation strategy during symptom provocation; human participants (OCD patients and controls); reports task-related BOLD activation results. No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study that used an emotion regulation paradigm asking participants to increase positive emotion; includes clinical (depressed) and healthy control groups and reports task-related brain activation/connectivity results (nucleus accumbens and fronto-striatal connectivity). All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract reports a task-based whole-brain fMRI study with 55 healthy human participants performing instructed regulation of negative emotion (and viewing without regulating). Task-related activation results are reported (GLM contrasts and task-rest interactions). No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the study used an implicit face-matching task (no instructions to regulate emotions) and included only bipolar patients without a separate control group. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1, I4. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I2 (no emotion regulation instruction), I3 (patient-only sample without a reported separate control group).

Task-based fMRI with human participants using emotion-regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression), including proactive/anticipation regulation; reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria met in the abstract.

Excluded because participants did not perform an emotion regulation task (I2 not met): they viewed emotional faces and made perceptual judgments without instruction to regulate. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human children sample), I4 (reports task-related activation). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI in healthy adult humans reporting task-related brain activation (ACC). The abstract does not specify that participants were instructed to perform an emotion regulation strategy (uncertain whether anticipation counts as regulation), so I2 is not demonstrated from abstract alone; include for full-text review to resolve.

Exclusion E2 met: this is an empathy/viewing fMRI study without instructions to amplify or dampen emotion (no regulation task). Inclusion I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), and I4 (task-related brain activation/connectivity results) are satisfied. Inclusion I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task) is not demonstrated in the abstract.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants, ages included), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 - abstract does not describe an emotion-regulation instruction or strategy (it reports attentional modulation via an affective Stroop, not explicit regulation).

No emotion regulation instructions are reported (I2 not met). The study is a task-based fMRI and reports task-related activations (I1, I4 met). It enrolls only VCFS patients without a separately reported control group (I3 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria clearly apply (none met).

EXCLUDED. No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (not an emotion-regulation task—participants performed prosody categorization/processing, not instructed to regulate emotion). Also does not address review objective of visual-stimulus emotion regulation (auditory speech prosody used).

Task-based fMRI of social risky decision-making in MDD; meets I1 (task fMRI), I3 (human clinical participants with controls), and I4 (reports task-related brain activations). Does not involve an emotion-regulation instruction/strategy or regulating responses to visual emotional stimuli, so I2 is not met. No exclusion criteria met.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI not stated in abstract), I2 (classical conditioning/nocebo paradigm is not an explicit emotion-regulation task), I4 (no report of task-related brain activation results in abstract). I3 (human participants) is not explicitly stated. Abstract lacks evidence of the required emotion-regulation fMRI paradigm, so exclude.

Resting-state fMRI study with no task-based emotion regulation or task-related activation reported. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). No exclusion criteria from the list apply.

E1 (non-empirical conceptual/review article): abstract describes a conceptual model and does not report original human task-based fMRI data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (human participants performing an emotion regulation task), I3 (participant groups reported), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

EXCLUDED: This is a resting-state fMRI study, not a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm. Inclusion met: I3 (clinical participants with control group). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results). Exclusion criteria: none met (not a review; not an empathy/perspective-taking task).

Task-based fMRI study of angry face processing in healthy human participants reporting task-related brain activations. The abstract does not state whether participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 uncertain). No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to determine if the task involved explicit emotion regulation or qualifies as passive viewing per the review objective.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of an emotion regulation task in human adolescents, reporting task-related neural measures (amygdala–rVLPFC functional connectivity) linked to anxiety. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in 54 healthy participants, reporting task-related functional connectivity alterations comparing reappraisal versus maintain. All inclusion criteria I1–I4 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI in healthy human participants that manipulates and reduces appetitive/emotional responses to visual food cues via an aversive aftertaste (a regulation-like cognitive control of appetite). Reports task-related brain activation. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports connectivity and treatment-response in major depression but does not describe a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI paradigm or task-related activation. Exclusion criteria: none met. Inclusion met: I3 (clinical participants). Inclusion not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation).

EXCLUDED: No evidence participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human adolescent participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Exclusion criteria met: none (E[]). The study used a social exclusion (Cyberball) paradigm assessing emotional responsivity, not an emotion regulation task.

Resting-state fMRI study without any task or emotion-regulation paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results).

Abstract reports an fMRI study of emotion processing/regulation in youth comparing bipolar subtypes and healthy controls, but does not specify whether participants performed an explicit emotion-regulation task (e.g., reappraisal) or details of stimuli. Insufficient information to confirm I2, so include for full-text review.

Abstract reports cognitive reappraisal of palatable food images in human participants across a BMI range and describes modulation of neural responsivity—matching emotion regulation of visual stimuli and task-related brain activation. The abstract does not explicitly state 'task-based fMRI', so include for full-text review to confirm imaging modality.

Study examines neural responses to nostalgia-evoking music (auditory stimuli) and does not involve participants performing an emotion regulation task; does not address regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (emotion regulation task). Exclusion criteria met: none.

Abstract describes analysis of multi-subject fMRI data with stimuli and mentions application to an emotion regulation study; exclusion criteria not met. Abstract lacks sufficient detail to confirm that participants performed an emotion-regulation task or that task-related activation results are reported, so include for full-text review.

Study is a voxel-based morphometry (structural MRI) investigation of gray matter in depressed female outpatients; it is not a task-based fMRI study and does not report task-related brain activation during emotion regulation. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (increase/maintain/decrease) of unpleasant pictures in human older adults and reports task-related BOLD activation in medial prefrontal regions and amygdala. No exclusion criteria are met. Satisfies inclusion criteria I1–I4; include for full-text review.

Study is an fMRI decision-making/ambiguity task, not an emotion regulation study. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation reported). Inclusion not met: I2 (emotion regulation task not present). Exclusion criteria: none met (E1, E2 not applicable).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in depressed youth and healthy controls, and reports task-related brain activation (amygdala, vmPFC). This satisfies the review inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met from the abstract.

Study is a structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) genetics study, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Exclusion based on lack of task fMRI and lack of emotion-regulation task or task-related activation reporting.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study (I1) using cognitive emotion regulation/reappraisal during reward anticipation (I2) in healthy human participants (I3) and reports task-related brain activation results (DLPFC, putamen, PPI) (I4). No exclusion criteria are met; include for full-text review.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study with task-related anterior insula activation during aversive anticipation (I1, I4) in human participants (I3). It is unclear whether participants performed an instructed emotion regulation task (I2) because effects relate to dispositional reappraisal rather than instructed regulation. Inclusion status is uncertain from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

This is a task-based fMRI study of human youth viewing emotional (negative) faces vs shapes (implicit emotion processing), reports task-related brain activation and includes clinical and control groups; the meta-analysis objective explicitly admits studies that view emotional stimuli without regulation, so the study is eligible for full-text review.

Study used structural (T1) MRI in healthy adults reporting hippocampal cell density. It is not a task-based fMRI study, does not involve an emotion-regulation task, and does not report task-related brain activation. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1, I2, I4.

Excluded because the study is a structural MRI morphometry study, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion-regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

E1 met: abstract describes conceptual/proposal paper on fMRI neurofeedback without reporting original human empirical data. No evidence of a task-based fMRI study or participants performing an emotion regulation task, nor task-related brain activation results. Inclusion criteria I1-I4 are not demonstrated and thus not met.
EXCLUDE: I2 not met — the study uses an Emotional Face Matching/processing task without instructions to regulate emotion; inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4; no exclusion criteria met.

EXCLUDE: Study uses resting-state fMRI rather than a task-based emotion regulation paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical participants with MDD). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation).

Abstract indicates an fMRI task involving observation of risk-taking actions and suggests investigation of emotion-related processing; it is unclear whether participants actively regulated emotions or merely viewed stimuli.
