Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I1) of cognitive reappraisal emotion regulation (I2) in human clinical (ASD) and control participants (I3), reporting task-related brain activation results (I4). No exclusion criteria evident.

Exclusion E1 applies: this is a study protocol without original human data or reported results. No inclusion criteria are clearly met: I1 not demonstrated (task-based fMRI not specified), I2 not demonstrated (no emotion-regulation task described), I3 not demonstrated (participant/control details unclear), I4 not met (no task-related brain activation results reported).

Adult human participants performed a cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task during task-based fMRI; task-related activation results are reported (vmPFC, extrastriate cortex); study includes a patient (obesity) and separate healthy control group. No exclusion criteria met.

Title and abstract state this is an fMRI study of emotion regulation in bipolar disorder type I with human clinical participants. However, the abstract lacks details on whether a task-based regulation paradigm was used vs passive viewing and whether task-related activation results are reported. Include for full-text review to confirm task details and reported activations.

Abstract reports an fMRI connectivity-based neurofeedback training in human participants targeting emotion regulation (increasing dmPFC→amygdala top-down connectivity) with associated behavioral changes (valence ratings). This indicates task-based fMRI and task-related brain results. It is unclear from the abstract whether the emotional stimuli were visual, so include for full-text review to verify specific review objective alignment.

Study uses EEG/ERP, not task-based fMRI (I1 not met), and does not instruct participants to regulate their emotion (no emotion regulation task; I2 not met). It includes human children (I3 met) and reports task-related brain activity via ERPs (I4 met). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

No task-based fMRI or emotion-regulation task reported. Study uses proton chemical shift imaging in developmental stuttering (metabolic/neuroimaging), not task-related fMRI activation. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human adolescent participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). The study reports resting-state functional connectivity rather than a task-based emotion regulation paradigm, so it does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

Excluded because this is an EEG/ERP study using N2 source estimates rather than a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human child participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (no clear evidence participants performed an explicit emotion regulation task; only emotion induction/inhibitory control). No exclusion criteria met.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical sample: comorbid depression and obesity). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (no task-based fMRI; study uses DTI/FA), I2 (no emotion regulation task; uses self-report ERQ and behavioral RTs), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported). Therefore exclude based on failure to meet core inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I4.

No evidence the task was an emotion-regulation task: fMRI compared scratching/picking vs caressing (tactile stimulation) rather than instructed regulation of emotional responses to stimuli. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical sample with control group), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (no demonstrated emotion-regulation instructions or paradigm). Exclusion criteria: none met.

No evidence in abstract of a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm or task-related activation results. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results), I3 (participant sample not specified in abstract).

Excluded because the study does not involve an emotion regulation task (I2 not met). It is a task-based fMRI study with healthy human participants and reports task-related activation (I1, I3, I4 met). No exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because abstract does not describe an emotion regulation task (I2 not met): the study examines decision-induced rationalization without instructions to regulate emotional responses. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activations). No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded because the study is not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (emotion-regulation-related task with negative emotion induction), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation via EEG/ERP and source modeling). Exclusion criteria met: none. The neural data are EEG/ERP (not fMRI), so it does not satisfy the fMRI requirement for this meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study in humans with generalized social anxiety disorder performing an emotion regulation task (attention regulation of negative self-beliefs) and reporting task-related neural activation results comparing MBSR vs aerobic exercise. It meets inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI (I1), human participants (I3), and task-related brain activation results (I4). It is unclear from the abstract whether participants were explicitly instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2). The study examines affective working memory and distractor interference, which could reflect emotion regulation or cognitive control of emotion; insufficient detail to confirm. Include for full-text review to determine if I2 is met.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participant groups spanning typical development, ADHD, ASD). Inclusion IDs not met / not demonstrated in abstract: I1 (task-based fMRI not described), I2 (no emotion regulation task described), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported). Abstract lacks evidence of an emotion-regulation fMRI task or task activation data.

No exclusion criteria met. The abstract reports cytokine and μ-opioid function in MDD and healthy volunteers but provides no evidence of a task-based fMRI, an emotion-regulation task, or task-related brain activation results. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants: MDD and healthy volunteers). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants reported), I4 (reports task-related brain activation — ERP). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not task-based fMRI; EEG/ERP study), I2 (not an emotion-regulation task).

Task-based fMRI study of depressed and control participants performing reappraisal (detachment/immersion) with reported amygdala and prefrontal activation differences. Meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract; include for full-text review.

Abstract does not report task-based fMRI or task-related brain activation results (I1 and I4 not met). It does involve human participants performing instructed emotion regulation (I2) and a human sample (I3). No exclusion criteria appear met.

EXCLUDED: The task (Multi-Source Interference Task) is a cognitive interference/inhibition task, not an emotion-regulation or emotion-viewing task. Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion not met: I2 (no emotion-regulation instruction or emotional stimuli). Exclusion criteria met: none (E1/E2 not applicable).

Excluded because the task involved negative autobiographical memory recall rather than regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli (does not meet the meta-analysis stimulus requirement). Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I2 (emotion regulation task), I3 (clinical human participants), I4 (reports neural/task-related activation). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (explicit task-based fMRI not specified) and the review-specific requirement for visual stimuli (not met).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of human participants performing emotion regulation of negative visual stimuli, examining SSRI effects and 5-HTTLPR moderation and reporting neural (fMRI) outcomes. This meets the review’s task, participant, and activation-report criteria. No exclusion criteria are indicated in the abstract.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study with adolescent human participants and task-related brain activation (I1, I3, I4). It does not clearly state participants were instructed to regulate emotion (I2 unclear); observed 'emotion regulation and mentalizing' may be spontaneous. No exclusion criterion is clearly met. Include for full-text review to determine whether an instructed emotion-regulation task was used or E2 applies.

Protocol paper (no original task-fMRI data reported) — exclusion E1. Abstract does not describe a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm nor report task-related activation, so I1, I2, and I4 are not demonstrated. It does describe a human clinical sample (recurrent MDD), so I3 is met.

Abstract investigates neural correlates of emotion regulation in BPD with patient and control groups, satisfying I3. The abstract does not explicitly state task-based fMRI (I1), that participants performed a defined emotion-regulation task (I2), or that task-related brain activation results are reported (I4). No exclusion criteria are met. Insufficient detail to determine inclusion from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (emotional Stroop task/processing of emotional stimuli), I3 (clinical phobia and control groups), I4 (reports task-related cortical activation). Inclusion criterion not met: I1 — task-based fMRI required but study used functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), so modality criterion fails.

Abstract reports a controlled fMRI study in patients with bipolar disorder, indicating human clinical participants with a control group (I3). However, it does not specify whether the fMRI was task-based, whether participants performed an emotion-regulation or visual-stimulus viewing task, or whether task-related activation results are reported (I1, I2, I4 unclear). Include for full-text review to determine task details and reported activations.

E1 (non-empirical review) applies: abstract describes brain circuitry and plasticity in a review/synthesis without original human task-based fMRI data or reported task activations. Inclusion criteria I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion-regulation task), and I4 (task-related brain activation results) are not met; I3 (participant groups) is not demonstrated.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in which SAD patients performed emotion-regulation tasks (breath-focused and distraction-focused attention) while reacting to negative self-beliefs and shows task-related brain activation changes (amygdala and attentional regions). It is unclear whether stimuli were visual and no control group is mentioned; insufficient information to exclude. Include for full-text review to confirm visual-stimuli requirement and presence/absence of separate control group.

Abstract describes task-based fMRI in human participants and reports neural activity to emotional stimuli (I1, I3, I4 appear met). It does not specify that participants performed an emotion regulation task (I2 not demonstrated). Inclusion is uncertain from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Excluded: study used EEG/ERP (LPP), not task-based fMRI, so I1 not met. It did not involve an instructed emotion regulation strategy (participants viewed pictures while performing math), so I2 not met. It does not report task-related fMRI activation results (I4 not met). It does include human participants (I3 met). No exclusion criteria were triggered.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study (I1) with an emotion reactivity and top-down regulation task (I2) and reports task-related brain activation results (I4). The abstract does not state whether a control group was included (I3 not demonstrated); no exclusion criteria met.

E2 met: study is an empathy/perspective-taking task without instructions to amplify or dampen participants' emotional responses. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation results). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an fMRI study; used fNIRS) and I2 (not an emotion-regulation task).

Excluded per E2: the task involves perspective-taking/self-other conditions (Your-Baby, Self, Just-Listen) without instructions to amplify or dampen emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and control groups), I4 (task-related activation results). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (participants were not instructed in emotion regulation strategies; study uses auditory perspective-taking rather than an explicit emotion-regulation task).

No task-based fMRI or task-related brain activation is reported. The study examines microstructural integrity (likely DTI) and associations between self-reported habitual cognitive reappraisal and symptoms in healthy young adults. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (no in-scanner emotion regulation task), I4 (no task-related activation results). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports an fMRI study in bipolar patients (clinical human sample) but does not specify a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm or clearly report task-related activation to emotional visual stimuli. Because inclusion status is uncertain from the abstract and no exclusion criteria are met, include for full-text review to determine whether I1, I2 and I4 are satisfied.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion I3 met (human children sample). Inclusion I1 not met: this is EEG/ERP study, not a task-based fMRI study required by the review. Inclusion I2 not demonstrated: placebo manipulation is not an instructed emotion-regulation task (e.g., reappraisal). Inclusion I4 not met for fMRI brain-activation reporting (EEG/ERP reported instead). Therefore excluded.

Task-based fMRI fear conditioning/extinction protocol constitutes a task involving viewing emotional (fear) stimuli (without instructed regulation) and reports task-related brain activation in human participants. Meets I1, I2 (viewing emotional stimuli/adjacent regulation domain), I3, and I4. No exclusion criteria met (not a non-empirical paper, not an empathy/perspective-taking study). Include for full-text review to confirm task details.

Included for full-text review: abstract reports task-based fMRI in never-depressed adults with reported amygdala hyper-reactivity (task-related activation). However the abstract does not specify an emotion regulation task, so I2 is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria met from abstract.

Task-based fMRI study in humans performing an explicit emotion regulation task (maintain/enhance/suppress) with patient (mTBI) and control groups and reporting task-related brain activation, meeting I1,I2,I3,I4; no exclusions met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (emotion regulation task: instructed suppression), I3 (human healthy adult participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation via ERP LPP). Inclusion criterion not met: I1 — study used EEG/ERP (LPP), not task-based fMRI, so it does not meet the meta-analysis modality requirement.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I2 (emotion regulation task), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related neural activation reported via LPP). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study — this is an EEG/ERP study). Excluded because the meta-analysis requires task-based fMRI studies.

EXCLUDE because this is a structural MRI study of trait expressive suppression, not a task-based fMRI emotion regulation experiment. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human healthy participants). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI study), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results).

No fMRI data and not an emotion regulation task: study uses EEG/ERN measures of error processing, not task-based fMRI, and does not involve regulating emotional responses. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation via EEG). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task).
Task-based fMRI study where human participants performed cognitive reappraisal of positive and negative visual images and reported task-related brain activation results; clearly meets I1–I4.

EXCLUDED: Not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met) and did not involve an emotion regulation task (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation via ERPs). No exclusion criteria met (none of E1–E2).

Abstract does not describe a task-based emotion regulation fMRI study. It reports network analyses of functional interactions (likely resting-state or non-regulation task), with no mention of regulating or viewing emotional visual stimuli or task-related activation. Inclusion met: I3 (older adult human participants). Inclusion not met: I1, I2, I4. Exclusion criteria: none met.

The study uses recall of an anger-inducing autobiographical memory (no visual stimuli), so it does not address the meta-analysis objective of regulating emotional responses to visual stimuli. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1, I2, I3, I4. Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli (study uses autobiographical recall).

Abstract reports fMRI in human OCD patients but does not specify whether task was a regulation or simple viewing task, nor whether task-related activation results are reported. Insufficient information to confirm I1, I2, I4; I3 (human clinical participants) is met. Include for full-text review to determine task and reported contrasts.

I2 not met: the task involves sadness introspection and judging nonemotional features, but participants were not instructed to regulate (e.g., reappraise, amplify, or dampen) their emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human adolescent sample), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Exclusion met: none (E1 and E2 not applicable). Therefore exclude due to failure to meet I2 (emotion regulation task).

Exclusion: none met. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants implied). Inclusion not met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; resting-state fMRI), I2 (not an emotion regulation task; measures dispositional optimism at rest), I4 (does not report task-related brain activation). Therefore excluded from this meta-analysis focused on task-based emotion regulation fMRI.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (reports task-related electrocortical/brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; uses electrocortical measures), I2 (does not describe an emotion regulation task—studies anticipation/processing), I3 (clinical VVS sample but abstract does not report a separate control group).

Excluded because the study used passive viewing of emotional pictures to measure amygdala habituation and did not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion not met: I2 (no emotion-regulation task). Exclusion criteria met: none.

Excluded because the study reports structural (grey matter volume) associations with habitual reappraisal rather than task-based fMRI activation. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (task-based fMRI) not met; I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task) not demonstrated; I4 (reports task-related brain activation results) not met. No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) are met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met: I1 (not task-based fMRI; uses resting-state fNIRS), I2 (not an emotion regulation task; stress induction/rumination measure), I4 (does not report task-related brain activation). Therefore excluded based on failure to meet required inclusion criteria.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activations). Inclusion criterion not met: I2 — the study examines generation/regulation of internally generated emotions, not regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli or viewing stimuli as required by the meta-analysis objective.

The study is task-based fMRI with OCD and control groups and reports task-related activation (I1, I3, I4). However, the task elicits shame and guilt via imagined scenarios and does not describe any emotion-regulation instructions (reappraisal, distancing, acceptance) or viewing/regulating of visual stimuli. Inclusion criterion I2 (emotion regulation task) is not demonstrated; no exclusion criteria are met.

E2 applies: This is an empathy/vicarious-pain study without instructions to amplify or dampen participants' emotional responses, so it does not meet the emotion-regulation requirement. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (emotion regulation task).
MEG study (not fMRI) and does not appear to involve an instructed emotion-regulation task; reports neural task activation in humans. Exclude because I1 and I2 are not met.

Abstract reports a human functional imaging study examining emotion regulation during an attention control task in bipolar I and II participants, implying task-based fMRI with neurophysiological (functional) results relevant to the review. No exclusion criteria are met and criteria I1–I4 appear satisfied based on the abstract.

Study is excluded because it is not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met) and does not examine an emotion regulation task (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation via ERPs). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) apply.

Excluded: study is not a task-based fMRI emotion regulation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs NOT met: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion-regulation task), I4 (does not report task-related fMRI activation results).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in human clinical groups (OCD and SAD) using emotional visual stimuli, satisfying I1 and I3. It does not specify whether participants performed an emotion-regulation task (I2) or clearly report task-related activation results (I4). Information is insufficient to determine inclusion, so include for full-text review.

Real-time fMRI neurofeedback is a task-based fMRI with human participants and the abstract indicates functional effects, satisfying I1, I3, and likely I4. The abstract does not indicate participants performed an emotion-regulation task in response to visual stimuli (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria met. Insufficient detail to confirm relevance to the review objective, so include for full-text review.

Excluded (E2): This is a task-based fMRI study (I1) with human participants (I3) reporting task-related activations (I4), but it measures mentalizing/perspective-taking without instruction to alter participants' emotional responses—fits exclusion E2; I2 (emotion-regulation task) not met or demonstrated.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal emotion regulation task in human participants and presents task-related brain activation results (vmPFC tracking of subjective and normative valence). No exclusion criteria are met.

Not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met) and does not report an emotion regulation task (I2 not met). It does involve human participants (I3) and reports task-related neural activation via ERPs (I4). No exclusion criteria met. Exclude for full-text review because the modality and task do not match the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

Abstract describes cognitive regulation of emotion-eliciting stimuli in anxious children, matching an emotion-regulation task (I2) and a clinical child sample (I3). The abstract does not explicitly state task-based fMRI or report task-related activation (I1 and I4 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm imaging modality and activation results.

Exclusion: none of the exclusion criteria apply. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical sample with separate controls). Inclusion NOT met: I1 (not task-based; resting-state fMRI), I2 (no emotion-regulation task), I4 (no task-related activation results reported). Therefore exclude.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and control groups), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion not met: I2 — this is a distress-tolerance PASAT task, not an emotion-regulation task involving instructed regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli; thus does not meet the meta-analysis’ emotion-regulation task criterion.

EXCLUDED: Study is not a task-based fMRI study and does not involve an emotion regulation task nor report task-related brain activation. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2).

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs clearly met: I2 (emotion regulation via distraction) and I4 (task-related brain activation reported via oxyHb changes). (c) Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 is not met — study used NIRS, not task-based fMRI; I3 not clearly demonstrated (participant details not specified). Therefore excluded due to I1 not met.

Animal histological study of lamprey brain using PCNA; not a human task-based fMRI emotion regulation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs NOT met: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no human emotion regulation task), I3 (not human participants), I4 (no task-related fMRI activation results).

Not an fMRI emotion-regulation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants implied by EEG/EEG on scalp). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (not an emotion-regulation task), I4 (reports EEG evoked potentials, not task-related fMRI activation results).

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in human participants and task-related brain activation during emotional discrimination, but it is unclear whether participants were explicitly instructed to regulate their emotional responses (reappraisal/other regulation) versus passive viewing/discrimination. Because I2 (emotion regulation task) is not clearly demonstrated, include for full-text review to confirm eligibility.

Excluded because inclusion criterion I2 (emotion regulation task) is not met: abstract describes mood induction and reward/frustration responses but no instruction to regulate emotion (e.g., reappraisal). Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Exclusion criteria met: [].

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI not clearly reported), I2 (no emotion regulation task described), I4 (no task-related activation results reported). Excluded: No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I3 (healthy human participants). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; this is EEG), I2 (no emotion-regulation task; study examines attentional control without regulation of emotional responses), I4 (does not report task-related fMRI activation results).

Not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met) and does not involve instructed emotion regulation (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation via EEG). No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2).

This is an animal (macaque) anatomical tracer study, not a human task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation. This is a theoretical/hypothesis paper without original human data (E1). It does not report task-based fMRI (I1), emotion-regulation tasks (I2), participant groups (I3), or task-related brain activation results (I4).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Study uses resting-state fMRI rather than a task-based emotion regulation or viewing task. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participant groups: LTAA and NSAC). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related activation results).

Abstract reports an emotion regulation task comparing brain activation across schizophrenia patients, non-affected siblings, and healthy controls, and thus addresses the review objective. It does not explicitly state fMRI or stimulus modality (visual) in the abstract, so full text is needed to confirm imaging modality and stimulus type. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a tDCS-fMRI study aiming to modulate implicit emotion regulation in human participants but does not clearly state a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation task or report task-related activation. Key inclusion criteria (I1, I2, I4) are uncertain from abstract alone, so INCLUDE for full-text review to clarify.

Abstract describes an empirical task-based fMRI study in humans with social anxiety disorder that examines anterior cingulate and amygdala activation during emotion regulation to predict CBT outcome, and reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met.

Study used magnetoencephalography (MEG), not task-based fMRI, and employed an NPU threat-predictability paradigm without instructions to regulate emotion. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants) and I4 (task-related brain activation reported). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I2 (emotion-regulation task). Does not address review objective: meta-analysis requires regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli, but this task used autobiographical memory recall (non-visual). Inclusion met: I1, I2, I3, I4. Exclusion met: none (E1/E2 not applicable).

Excluded because the study is not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met), does not involve an explicit emotion-regulation instruction/task (I2 not met), and does not report task-related brain activation results from fMRI (I4 not demonstrated). Task-based fMRI study measuring BOLD responses to unpleasant (sport-specific and general) images in athletes and controls; reports task-related activation (prefrontal cortex, insula). Task-based fMRI study examining acceptance as an emotion-regulation strategy in individuals with BPD; reports neural correlates (brain activation). Fits inclusion criteria I1–I4 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in human 4–6-year-old children examining functional brain activity related to emotion regulation. It is unclear whether participants were instructed to explicitly regulate emotions, so include for full-text review to confirm I2.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related neural activation/connectivity). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I2 (no evidence participants were instructed to regulate emotional responses; study used a fear conditioning task), I3 (clinical sample only; no separate control group reported).

Task-based fMRI in human participants with alcohol use disorder examining cognitive regulation of craving and negative emotion, reporting PFC recruitment and neural mechanisms (task-related brain activation). Meets I1, I2, I3, I4; no exclusion criteria apparent.

Study uses EEG/ERP (N2) and source-estimated ROIs, not task-based fMRI, so I1 (task-based fMRI) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (emotion regulation task), I3 (human children participants), I4 (task-related brain activation reported). No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded because the study used magnetoencephalography (not task-based fMRI; I1 not met) and examines neural responses to negative stimuli without evidence of an emotion regulation task (I2 not met). Fails key inclusion criteria: this is a PET study (O-15 water) not an fMRI task (I1 not met) and does not report an emotion-regulation task (no cognitive reappraisal or similar; I2 not met). EXCLUDED: This is an EEG study of motor processing in adolescents, not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

EXCLUDE: Not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met), did not report task-related brain activation (I4 not met), and did not involve an emotion-regulation task during fMRI (I2 not met). Study involved healthy human participants (I3 met). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract describes behavioral eye-tracking with self-report; no fMRI or brain-activation results reported. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (cognitive reappraisal task), I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation results).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in healthy human participants, with voxelwise task-related brain activation results (PFC and amygdala). This satisfies inclusion criteria I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

The abstract describes a task-based fMRI study examining emotional reactivity and regulation in PTSD patients and links brain activation to treatment outcome. This meets inclusion criteria I1-I4. No exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract. Visual-stimulus specifics are not explicit but the study aligns with emotion regulation constructs relevant to the review.

Not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not task-based fMRI; uses QEEG), I2 (not an emotion-regulation task; participants viewed colored rooms without regulation instructions), I4 (does not report task-related fMRI activation).

Task-based fMRI with human participants viewing religious vs nonreligious images during painful stimulation; contemplation of the religious image led to emotional detachment (an emotion-regulation-like process) and the paper reports task-related brain activations (right VLPFC). Fits inclusion criteria for emotion regulation to visual stimuli and reports brain activation results.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study investigating emotion regulation in ADHD, matching the review objective. However, it does not specify whether a separate control group was reported or explicitly state task-related activation results in the abstract. Include for full-text review to confirm control group reporting and reported activation results.

Abstract provides insufficient methodological detail to determine whether this is a task-based fMRI study reporting task-related activation during an emotion regulation task. Title suggests neural measures of emotion regulation, but inclusion criteria I1–I4 are not demonstrated in the abstract. Include for full-text review to confirm whether task-based fMRI and task activation results are reported.

Study is excluded because it does not address the review objective: participants regulated emotion during autobiographical memory recall rather than in response to visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation via cognitive reappraisal), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activation). No exclusion criteria met (none).

Study is PET imaging of serotonin receptor binding after ECT, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) apply.

The study does not manipulate or instruct emotion regulation (it used an emotional declarative memory/encoding task), so I2 (emotion regulation task) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (clinical group with controls), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria apply (E1,E2 not met).

Study uses Cyberball to measure neural responses to social exclusion but does not indicate participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses. Thus it does not meet the emotion-regulation task criterion (I2).

Study used resting-state fMRI and magnetic resonance spectroscopy, not a task-based emotion regulation paradigm. Inclusion I3 (human participants with control group) is met. Inclusion I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), and I4 (task-related activation results) are not met or not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

No evidence the task involved active emotion regulation. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human adolescent clinical sample with NSSI), I4 (reports neural responses to emotional stimuli). Inclusion not met: I2 — study examined automatic processing of masked emotional faces with no instruction to regulate emotions. Exclusion criteria: none (E1,E2 not met).

Task-based fMRI using visual negative-emotion pictures with induced heat pain to probe pain-mediated affect regulation; includes clinical (BPD) and control groups; reports task-related neural results (amygdala activation/deactivation and connectivity). Fits inclusion (viewing or regulating) and no exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because study used fNIRS (not task-based fMRI) and did not involve an emotion regulation instruction. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (not fMRI—used fNIRS), I2 (no emotion regulation task—participants judged emotion/speed rather than regulating their emotions).

Patient-only fMRI neurofeedback study (Patients n=10) with no separately reported control group in the abstract. Inclusion criterion not met/not demonstrated: I3 (no control group reported for the patient sample). Exclusion criteria: none met (E1,E2 not applicable).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in human patients performing an emotion regulation task (cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative affect), and reports task-related brain activation results. This satisfies inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria are met.

Event-related fMRI study with human participants doing a voluntary emotion regulation task (maintain vs passively view negative/neutral pictures) and reporting task-related amygdala activation; meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apparent.

Excluded because the study does not meet I2: no emotion-regulation task was performed during fMRI (pressure-evoked pain used to assess CBT effects). Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Exclusion criteria met: none.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study where human participants used cognitive reappraisal to regulate cravings (personal-food images), and reports task-related neural activation (frontoparietal network, multivariate analyses). No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in humans performing cognitive emotion regulation (CER) during aversive visual processing and reports task-related brain activation/network results; no exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to extract detailed contrasts and participants.

Title and abstract indicate a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation in 41 adolescent girls, reporting disrupted amygdala–prefrontal connectivity linking stress-reactive rumination and depressive symptoms, which implies task-related neural results. Meets I1–I4 based on abstract information.

No evidence this is a task-based fMRI study or involves an emotion-regulation task; the abstract describes graph-theoretical analysis of functional network connectivity (likely resting-state) and does not report task-related activation. Exclusion IDs: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation).

Excluded: Study used resting-state fMRI rather than a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not task-based fMRI — resting-state), I2 (no emotion-regulation task reported), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported).

EXCLUDED because the study investigates neural substrates of visual exploration/saccades, not emotion regulation. Exclusion criteria met: none. Task-based fMRI study using Emotion Regulation Task (experience and regulation) and an emotional face perception task; reports task-related amygdala and insula activation and their change with treatment, directly addressing emotion regulation/perception of visual stimuli. Study is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting task-related activation (meets I1, I3, I4) but does not involve an emotion-regulation task with visual stimuli or instruction to regulate affect (does not meet I2). No exclusion criteria are triggered (none of E1–E2 apply).

Abstract provides insufficient information to determine whether a task-based emotion regulation paradigm was used or whether task-related activation results relevant to the meta-analysis are reported. No evidence that participants engaged in an emotion regulation task (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (clinical + control groups), I4 (task-related activation reported). Exclusion criteria met: none. Therefore exclude because one required inclusion criterion (I2) is not satisfied from abstract.

Task-based fMRI study (N=26) of primiparous mothers using distraction to regulate emotions in response to infant crying; reports reduced amygdala activation with regulation. Satisfies I1,I2,I3,I4. No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI reported in Study 2), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation results reported). This is a task-based fMRI study in humans using an established emotion regulation strategy (distancing/reappraisal), includes a clinical group (AN) with healthy controls, and reports task-related neural activation results (ventral striatum) linked to behavioral/EMA outcomes. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI in humans measuring amygdala activation/habituation to repeated unpleasant images pre- and post-12-month DBT; reports task-related brain activation. Abstract does not explicitly state an emotion-regulation instruction, but the review objective admits passive viewing studies, so inclusion is appropriate.

Excluded: study used resting-state fMRI (not task-based), does not involve an emotion-regulation task or viewing/regulating emotional visual stimuli, and does not report task-related activation. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1, I2, I4.

Randomized, placebo-controlled task-based fMRI in human participants assessing distraction as an emotion regulation strategy in PTSD patients and controls; reports task-related brain activation and functional connectivity results (thalamus, striatum, amygdala). Abstract provides insufficient information to confirm task-based fMRI, specific emotion regulation task, visual stimuli, or reported brain activation. Include for full-text review to determine if inclusion criteria I1–I4 are met.

Task-based fMRI with human adults using instructed emotion regulation (increase/decrease negative responses) during a task; reports ACC activation and connectivity related to errors (task-related brain activation). Fits inclusion criteria I1-I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract provides insufficient methodological detail to confirm inclusion: it does not state whether task-based fMRI was used, whether participants performed an instructed emotion-regulation task during fMRI, or whether task-related brain activation results are reported. Task-based fMRI in humans viewing masked emotional (happy/fearful) faces; reports task-related activation differences in anterior cingulate and amygdala. No task-based fMRI or emotion-regulation task reported (SPECT used during mutism); not a task-based fMRI study and no task-related fMRI activation results. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met: I1, I2, I4. No exclusion criteria met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical sample: youth with ADHD). Task-based fMRI with SZ and matched controls; reports task-related brain activation (left IFG) during emotional distractors and WM load. Abstract reports task-based fMRI in human children/adolescents with task-related brain activation to emotional conflict, but does not indicate an explicit emotion-regulation instruction (I2 not demonstrated). Abstract reports an effective connectivity fMRI study in bipolar patients (human clinical sample: I3). Task-based fMRI study examining voluntary attentional regulation of emotion (an emotion regulation strategy) and emotion recognition in depressed patients and controls; reports activation and connectivity results. Excluded because the task is response inhibition (stop-signal), not an emotion-regulation task. Exclusion IDs met: none. Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of affect labeling (an incidental emotion-regulation strategy) with human participants and task-related neural activation results (frontal regions, amygdala). Abstract indicates an fMRI study in psychiatric patients linking stigma resistance with emotion regulation, but does not state a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm or report task-related activation results. Title/abstract indicate a task-based fMRI study in human patients (women with BPD) investigating emotional modulation of response inhibition, but the abstract does not specify whether participants performed an explicit emotion-regulation task or only viewed emotional stimuli, nor does it give task-related activation details. Abstract describes an fMRI/EEG randomized trial of CBT for aggression in children/adolescents but does not specify an emotion-regulation task (e.g., reappraisal) or report task-related activation results. Abstract does not specify use of task-based fMRI or report task-related brain activation; it examines frontal control over social-emotional actions predicting HPA-axis stress responsivity in humans, which could reflect an emotion-regulation-related task but is unclear. Patient-only sample with no separate control group reported, so inclusion criterion I3 is not met. The study used resting-state fMRI in healthy men and assessed trait anger via questionnaire; it does not involve a task-based emotion regulation paradigm or task-related activation results. Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of facial emotion processing in human youth at high risk for substance use, reporting neural activation. Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study reporting task-related brain activation and connectivity in human participants (unaffected bipolar offspring and controls). Include for full-text review to confirm whether an emotion-regulation instruction/strategy was used.

The abstract describes a structural neuroimaging study of resilience in police officers and does not report a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm or task-related activation results. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria explicitly met.

Abstract reports passive viewing of fearful faces and correlational analyses with trait optimism, not an instructed emotion-regulation task. No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study using an affective face-processing task (likely passive viewing), with social anxiety disorder participants; reports task-related activation (left amygdala) and functional connectivity changes pre/post iCBT. The abstract reports a human, task-based rtfMRI neurofeedback study that measured behavioral (pain empathy) and neural (activity, connectivity) outcomes, satisfying I1, I3 and I4. Abstract describes a task-based fMRI emotion regulation study (amygdala neurofeedback during aversive-picture viewing) reporting task-related activation and connectivity, but it does not indicate whether a control group is reported for this clinical BPD sample (I3 not demonstrated). Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using an emotion inhibition (regulation) task in human MDD patients and healthy controls, and reports task-related brain activation results (FWE-corrected). This meets inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the study reports resting-state fMRI connectivity in veterans, not a task-based emotion-regulation or stimulus-viewing fMRI. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results). No exclusion criteria met (none of E1/E2 apply).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (clinical human participants with MDD). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). Study is a task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive reappraisal in human participants (69 female adults), reporting task-related brain activation correlated with real-life affect. It meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are apparent from the abstract.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I1); participants performed an implicit emotion regulation task (I2); includes clinical SAD group and healthy controls reported separately (I3); reports task-related brain activation/connectivity results (PPI amygdala-vmPFC) and pre/post treatment changes (I4). Study used resting-state functional connectivity in MDD patients and controls, not a task-based emotion regulation fMRI paradigm. Inclusion criteria met: none. This study is a task-based fMRI fear-conditioning connectivity study in human participants that reports task-related activations (meets I1, I3, I4). Abstract does not specify a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI paradigm or report task-related activation; it likely examines amygdala connectivity (possibly resting-state). Insufficient information to determine whether inclusion criteria I1-I4 are met; include for full-text review.

Abstract reports adolescent human participants and associations of OFC connectivity with mood/anxiety in marijuana users, but does not specify a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI paradigm or report task-related activation. Task-based real-time fMRI neurofeedback study in human adolescents (7–16) teaching up-/down-regulation of an emotion-regulation region (insula); reports task-related activation and connectivity. Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans (12 females, 12 males) performing emotion regulation (view vs regulate emotional responses to pictures) and reports task-related brain activation results. Study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy human (female) participants performing voluntary emotion regulation of emotional pictures and reports task-related brain activation results; matches I1, I2, I3, and I4. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a film-based emotion reactivity and regulation task performed in an MRI scanner, with age-related changes in emotional reactivity and reported brain activation (middle frontal gyrus). Fits task-based fMRI emotion regulation studies; no exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study with human participants performing active down-regulation of emotional responses to unpleasant pictures (emotion regulation). Reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria met based on abstract.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an empirical task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs a cognitive emotion regulation strategy (distancing reappraisal) during stimulus presentation (I6). The emotional stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7). The sample includes a participant group (male marijuana users) with matched controls and reports group-level results (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation and unregulated viewing (e.g., "distance > baseline", "spontaneous_negative > baseline") (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-level FWE and peak coordinates are reported in standard (MNI) space (I10), and results are clearly described in text, figures, and coordinate lists (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not non-empirical (E3), not ROI-only (E4), not connectivity-only without task activation (E5), not only between-group contrasts without within-group effects (E6), and not an empathy/perspective paradigm without emotion-regulation instruction (E7).

No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-task contrasts are reported. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The paper reports within-task contrasts (fear regulate > attend; OCD regulate > attend; fear > neutral; OCD > neutral) and within-group regulation effects (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (no review-only, ROI-only, or connectivity-only reporting; within-group effects are reported; not an empathy/perspective-only task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) during presentation of visual stimuli (complex social images/IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts (RGT > fixation; RGT > AUT) and whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses with voxelwise FWE correction and reported activation coordinates/figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and the study should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed cognitive reappraisal (I6) using visual IAPS images (I7) in a healthy adult sample (I8) and reports a within-task contrast (ReappNeg vs LookNeg) (I9). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise map with coordinates). Exclusion criteria met: E4. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs participants in two regulation-related conditions (attention shifting: indoor/outdoor; appraisal/labeling: like/dislike) in addition to an implicit viewing condition. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This full text meets the review’s criteria for inclusion as an unregulated viewing fMRI study. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only analyses, or empathy/perspective-taking tasks) apply. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion as an unregulated visual-emotion task with whole-brain activation contrasts.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (‘Think Objectively’ vs ‘Watch’) using visual IAPS images in a within-subject randomized design. Sample is healthy adults and the full text contains methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Although this is a task-based fMRI study with an instructed reappraisal/perspective-taking regulation strategy (meets I5, I6), includes an appropriate sample (I8), reports within-task regulation-related contrasts (I9) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses/coordinates (I10, I11), it does NOT meet the required stimulus modality criterion: the emotional content consists of monetary decision outcomes and numeric gamble displays rather than visual emotional stimuli (e.g., IAPS images, faces, or film/video). The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs participants to use cognitive regulation (consider long-term consequences vs. immediate consumption) while viewing visual food images. It reports within-task regulation contrasts (LATER > NOW and related contrasts), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected statistics, and includes full methods, results, and discussion. Sample (healthy adult women) is eligible. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis eligibility for emotion regulation fMRI with visual stimuli and instructed cognitive control.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) and also includes an attentional-control implicit regulation task. Stimuli are visual (IAPS images and facial photographs). The sample is healthy adults. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise > Look-Negative; Threat Low > Threat High) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and FWE correction. Results and methods are fully reported in the main text. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; reports within-group task effects; not an empathy/perspective-taking-only study). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use two emotion-regulation strategies (Observe — a mindfulness/acceptance instruction — and Suppress) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Suppress-negative vs. Look-negative; Observe-negative vs. Look-negative; Look-negative vs. Look-neutral) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and thresholding described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the review (task-based fMRI, instructed regulation, visual stimuli, any sample, within-task contrasts, whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive self-distancing/reappraisal) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures). The methods describe standard SPM8 whole-brain preprocessing and GLM contrasts (e.g., US-Paired: CER>NoCER) used to define PFC seeds and report ROI coordinates (ventral striatum center x=26,y=6,z=-8), and the Results present within-task regulation contrasts and connectivity effects. The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria apply (no non-empirical article, not limited to only ROI/connectivity without whole-brain task maps, and within-task contrasts are reported). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of instructed emotion regulation of visual stimuli.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli in an adolescent sample and reports whole-brain, group-level contrasts (appetitive > aversive) with peak coordinates. However, participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); rather, they performed an inhibitory go/no-go task while emotional images were presented as incidental distractors. Therefore the study does not meet inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy). All other relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11), and no exclusion criteria from the list apply. Because I6 is not met, the study must be excluded.

Full-text reports a task-based fMRI study using instructed cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs Look conditions) with visual IAPS images, single-trial/block contrasts (Look-Negative>Look-Neutral; Reappraise>Look-Neutral), and a whole-brain voxelwise group-level analysis reporting MNI peak coordinates and cluster-corrected results. The sample includes a clinical GAD group and healthy controls with results reported separately. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; therefore complete. Meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This full text describes an empirical, task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts indexing emotion generation (Maintain>Observe) and regulation (Regulate>Maintain), and presents group-level analyses and peak coordinates (including one-sample/group activation maps used to create masks and reported peak coordinates and MNI values for seeds). Although some between-group tests used masks, group-level task activation maps and coordinate peaks are reported, and PPI connectivity is supplemental rather than the sole analysis. Sample and exclusions are described and a control group is reported separately. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI/small-volume results or only connectivity analyses) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the record is complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (film clips). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > watch-negative; suppress > watch-negative; watch-negative > watch-neutral) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported peak coordinates and tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and acceptance) during presentation of visual sad images (IAPS and normed photos). The sample includes remitted MDD and control participants with separate group analyses. The paper reports within-task contrasts (accept > reappraise, accept > view, reappraise > view) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported cluster results/locations in tables and text. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Although an a priori mask/SVC was noted for some analyses, whole-brain clusters outside frontal/amygdala (e.g., insula) are reported, supporting whole-brain task-evoked results. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI experiment that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) and also includes a placebo regulation condition. Visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures) were used. The sample comprises healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g. RU–CUR, PU–CUP and related conjunction/subtraction contrasts) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates and tables/figures in standard space. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, non-empirical paper, or empathy-only perspective tasks) are met. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal and imagery) during viewing of visual IAPS pictures. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (reappraise > maintain; change image > maintain; maintain > just look), includes whole-brain group-level analyses with peak MNI coordinates (tables/figures), and provides complete methods, results, and discussion. Sample and analyses meet inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met.

The full text reports an original, task-based fMRI experiment using an instructed emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). Participants include clinical (PTSD) and combat-exposed control groups with group-level analyses reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise > Maintain) and unregulated viewing contrasts (Maintain > Look), and provides whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates and corrected thresholds. The manuscript includes complete methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual, static disorder-related and neutral scene stimuli presented during a feature-based task (CDTD). The paper reports within-task contrasts of unregulated viewing (disorder-related > neutral) and an exploratory whole-brain analysis with reported activation clusters/tables, and includes both a clinical (SAD) group and healthy controls. No instructed emotion-regulation strategy was used, but the review objective allows inclusion of studies that merely view visual emotional stimuli without regulation. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis criteria for unregulated viewing contrasts. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

Full text reports an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (DECREASE vs LOOK) during presentation of visual IAPS images (static pictures). Sample and methods are appropriate; within-task regulation contrasts (decrease-negative > look-negative) and unregulated viewing contrasts (look-negative > look-neutral) are reported. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FWE-corrected maps and peak coordinates cited). Full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an original, task-based fMRI study using a visual emotional task (approach–avoidance with happy/angry face images) in human participants (police recruits). The task includes explicit instructions requiring cognitive control over automatic emotional action tendencies (incongruent vs. congruent blocks), and the primary neural contrasts reported (incongruent > congruent) index instructed emotional control. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected results, and also reports psychophysiological-interaction connectivity analyses. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for task-based fMRI of instructed emotion regulation/control with visual stimuli and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain results.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s stimulus and whole-brain reporting requirements. It is a task-based fMRI study with instructed self-regulation (rtfMRI neurofeedback using autobiographical recall) and reports within-task contrasts and ROI/effective-connectivity results; however, the regulated stimuli are internally generated autobiographical memories rather than externally presented visual emotional stimuli (violating I7). The paper focuses on ROI-based and effective-connectivity (VAR/SVAR) analyses and does not present a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-activation map with peak coordinates (violating I10) and thus falls under exclusions for reporting only ROI/seed-based connectivity/effective-connectivity results (E5) and ROI-only/partial-coverage results (E4). Therefore it fails required inclusion criteria and meets exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5); uses an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (distancing: close vs. far), qualifying as perspective-taking/reappraisal (I6); employs visual stimuli (video clips) (I7); sample is acceptable (young-adult smokers) (I8); reports within-task contrasts related to regulation and unregulated viewing (e.g., close vs. far; smoke vs. non-smoke) (I9); presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses registered to standard space with cluster-corrected maps (I10); and reports results in figures/tables/supplement (I11). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (‘‘decrease’’ vs ‘‘look’’) using visual IAPS images, satisfying the emotion-regulation task and stimulus requirements. The sample (PTSD patients with a randomized waiting-list control) is acceptable and group results are reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (decrease > look) and provides voxel-wise, whole-brain longitudinal analyses (with supplemental tables/figures of coordinates), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; includes whole-brain results beyond ROIs; reports within-group task effects in addition to interactions). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets I5–I11 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on instructed emotion regulation to visual stimuli.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (face-matching with fear and neutral faces) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (fear > neutral, fear > neutral+control) at the group level. The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion; second-level whole-brain analyses and coordinate labeling are reported (tables/figures and supplementary material). The sample is described and eligible. The meta-analysis objective accepts either instructed regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts; this study supplies unregulated viewing contrasts appropriate for inclusion and does not violate any exclusion criteria (it is empirical, reports whole-brain task-evoked maps, and is not ROI-only or connectivity-only). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) during an fMRI Ultimatum Game and during IAPS training, fulfilling the review focus on instructed emotion regulation. Stimuli are visual (IAPS pictures in training and photographs of proposers/faces during the task). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Down > Look, Down < Look < Up, regulated decisions contrasts) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. Participant sample is healthy adults and methods/results/discussion are fully presented. No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or perspective-taking without regulation) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and distraction) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and matched photos). It reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > look negative; distract > look negative), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and tables, and ROI analyses. Sample is described (18 healthy women). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no non-empirical paper, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation). Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (provided content is essentially an abstract). From the provided text, the study meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation task), I7 (visual stimuli: pictures), I8 (eligible sample), and I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts: increase/decrease vs no-change). This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal during viewing of visual stimuli (IAPS), includes both bipolar patients and healthy controls reported separately, and reports within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraising > attending-negative). Group-level whole-brain GLM analyses are described with cluster- and voxelwise thresholds and activation coordinate tables (Tables S3/S4), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Although the paper also includes effective connectivity (DCM) analyses, whole-brain task activation maps and contrasts relevant to emotion regulation are present. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the record is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise-Neg vs Maintain-Neg), uses visual stimuli (static facial images), reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation, and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported activations/coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study with instructed cognitive reappraisal of visual (video) stimuli and reports results separately for SAD patients and healthy controls (meets I5, I6, I7, I8). However, the paper presents ROI-based network (DEPNA) connectivity analyses and does not report any group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-activation maps with peak coordinates in standard space. Thus it fails the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results (I10 not met). Because the imaging results are reported only as ROI/seed-based connectivity (DEPNA) without accompanying whole-brain activation maps, this study meets exclusion criteria E4 and E5 (ROI-only/partial-coverage/connectivity-only reporting). Also, the paper does not provide the conventional within-task whole-brain activation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look) as voxelwise maps (I9 not satisfied for whole-brain contrast reporting). Therefore it should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal (reappraise > attend contrast) while viewing visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise Negative > Attend Negative; View Negative > View Neutral) and whole-brain group-level analyses with tables of activation peaks and ROI analyses. The sample (high-risk and control young women) is acceptable. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to apply emotion-regulation strategies (mindfulness and a cognitive reappraisal “reality checking”) during the anticipation and perception of emotional pictures. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., exp ng > nt, per ng > nt), presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and tables/figures of activations, and provides full Methods, Results, and Discussion. Sample is healthy adults. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (Cyberball) and reports whole-brain group analyses of a within-task contrast (rejection > acceptance), it does not meet the requirement that an emotion-regulation strategy be instructed during the task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports within-task/unregulated viewing contrast: rejection>acceptance), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; the study assesses dispositional mindfulness rather than instructing participants to regulate). Excluded because the study does not meet inclusion criterion I6: participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, instructed up-/down-regulation). This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal (maintain vs. reappraise) while viewing visual IAPS images. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed cognitive reappraisal using visual IAPS images in a clinical sample and reports the within-task contrast ReappNeg > LookNeg (meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). This places the study into exclusion category E4 (only ROI-based results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete.

This full-text fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) that instructs emotion regulation strategies including cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) and distraction (I6). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation and unregulated viewing (e.g., down-regulation > look, up-regulation > look, look aversive > look neutral) (I9). Group-level whole-brain analyses were conducted and reported (exploratory whole-brain results and MNI coordinates are provided for multiple contrasts), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I10). Results and whole-brain/ROI findings are described in text and tables/supplements (I11). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical task-based fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. I5: It is a task-based fMRI study with pre- and post-training scans. This is an fMRI neurofeedback task with instructed regulation (recall of positive autobiographical memories) in a clinical sample and whole-brain voxelwise analyses, but the regulated emotional stimuli are internally-generated memories rather than external VISUAL stimuli (no IAPS/images/film clips). This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use self-focused cognitive reappraisal (distancing, increase, decrease) while viewing visual IAPS images. This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment (Experiment 3) in which participants were instructed to cognitively reappraise visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) with explicit Increase/Maintain/Decrease instructions. This is a task-based fMRI study in adolescents using visual stimuli (faces) and an instructed regulation strategy (recall of positive autobiographical memories to upregulate affect during viewing of happy self-faces).
