This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs emotion regulation (diminish/enhance/maintain) using a cognitive reappraisal-like strategy (imagining less/more negative outcomes). Full text is complete. Met inclusion: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: facial images), I8 (eligible sample: healthy adults), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates), I11 (results reported clearly in text/tables). Not met: I6 — the task did NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraise, down-regulate, accept). Instead, the Cued Emotional Conflict Task required cognitive control/response mapping (respond to actual vs. opposite emotion) and the study correlated habitual ERQ scores with task activation; participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses in-scanner. I9 — there is no within-task contrast that reflects an instructed emotion-regulation condition (e.g., “reappraise > look”, “down-regulate > maintain”) nor a standard unregulated viewing contrast of emotion versus baseline that maps onto passive viewing; the reported contrasts index cognitive control/conflict (opposite vs actual) rather than an explicit regulation instruction. Therefore the study does not satisfy the core requirement (I6) and is excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) using an instructed emotion-regulation paradigm (cognitive reappraisal; I6) with visual stimuli (static IAPS pictures; I7). The sample includes unmedicated panic-disorder patients and healthy controls with results reported (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g., Reappraise vs Maintain, Maintain vs Reappraise; I9). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with standard-space coordinates and Z-values (MNI peaks cited; I10/I11). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Given the clear match to the review objective (fMRI emotion regulation to visual stimuli) and the presence of whole-brain task contrasts, the study should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (reappraise and distract) while participants view sad images (visual stimuli). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Sad-Reappraise > Sad-View, Sad-Distract > Sad-View) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise mixed-effects analyses in MNI space with tables/figures of cluster results. The sample and analyses meet eligibility and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-only, not empathy-without-regulation). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) during presentation of visual emotional images (IAPS and Internet pictures). The sample (healthy adult women) is acceptable. The paper reports within-task contrasts of regulation conditions (e.g., REAP vs ESUP, NAT vs REAP), behavioral and fMRI results, and second-level random-effects whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates and tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study should be excluded because the emotional stimuli being regulated are non-visual (anticipation of somatosensory pain via intraepidermal electrical stimulation), which fails inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be VISUAL). The study does meet multiple inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive reappraisal during anticipation), I8 (eligible sample: healthy participants reported separately), I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to regulation, e.g., regulation vs. anxiety), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), and I11 (results/coordinates described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded due to not meeting I7 (non-visual regulated stimuli).

This study used an implicit/incidental reappraisal manipulation (prior descriptions) but participants were not explicitly instructed to use an emotion regulation strategy. Inclusion criterion I6 requires that an emotion regulation strategy be instructed; that requirement is not met. All other relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied: task-based fMRI (I5), visual stimuli (I7), eligible sample (I8), within-task regulation-related contrast (NNEG-DESC > NEG-DESC) reported (I9), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported (I10), and acceptable reporting of whole-brain results (I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to meet I6 (no instructed regulation).

This is a task-based fMRI study with explicit instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal REAP and suppression ESUP) and a natural viewing condition. Emotional stimuli are visual static images (IAPS and photos) with social/nonsocial categories. Sample includes 19 healthy adults. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., social pleasant vs nonsocial pleasant; effects during NAT, REAP, ESUP) and whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with reported peak coordinates and SPM maps. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (reinterpretation) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > Negative; Negative > Reappraise), behavioral indices of reappraisal success, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and FDR correction. An ROI analysis on amygdala is also reported, but whole-brain results are present. Sample (undergraduate high vs low psychosis proneness) is acceptable. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

Full text is complete. Exclusion based on stimulus modality: the study uses scrambled sentences (visual words/sentences) as emotional stimuli, which violates inclusion criterion I7 (studies must use visual images/films; studies using word/sentence stimuli are excluded). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI/CASL perfusion task imaging), I6 (an instructed regulation condition present: explicit instruction to avoid negative sentences), I8 (sample reporting group-level results in healthy adults), I9 (within-task contrasts reported, e.g. emotional vs. neutral; interaction effects), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates), I11 (coordinates and maps clearly reported). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Therefore EXCLUDED because I7 not met (regulated stimuli are sentences/words).

All inclusion criteria are met: This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs explicit imagery-focused emotion regulation strategies (Relax, Excite) during a cue phase (I6). The regulated stimuli are visual (pictures of a slot machine and stamp machine) (I7). The sample is healthy adult participants (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts and behavioral/neural comparisons of Relax vs Look (regulation vs natural) with statistical tests (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (parametric GLM, FDR threshold) and peak coordinates/clusters are reported (e.g., Table 2 and coordinates cited) satisfying whole-brain evidence (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no review-only paper, not ROI-only, reports task activation maps, not only connectivity, and not an empathy-only paradigm). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore INCLUDE for the review.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of instructed cognitive reappraisal using visual stimuli in children (meets I5, I6, I7, I8), the published results focus exclusively on seed-based task functional connectivity (PPI) analyses and do not report any group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space. This study therefore reports only seed-based connectivity/effective connectivity results without accompanying whole-brain activation maps, which meets exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria I9 and I10 (within-task whole-brain activation contrasts and whole-brain peak coordinates) are not satisfied in the provided full text.

This article is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Regulate vs Look) during presentation of visual stimuli (static food images). It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Regulate > Look, Regulate Craved > Look Craved) and unregulated viewing contrasts, and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates and tables, using appropriate multiple-comparison correction. Sample includes healthy adults and individual-difference analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (not merely abstract/metadata). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and should be included.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of instructed cognitive reappraisal using visual IAPS images in older adults and reports within-task regulation contrasts, the reported analyses are ROI-based only. The methods and results describe a priori ROI GLM contrasts and ROI tables; no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space are reported. This means the study reports only ROI results without an accompanying whole-brain analysis, which meets exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation — cognitive reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli — IAPS images), I8 (sample allowed — older adults), I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts). Inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps with peak coordinates) is not met. Therefore the study must be excluded under E4.

The full text describes a task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were instructed to use emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) while viewing visual stimuli (Chinese Affective Picture System images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraisal vs. watch; suppression vs. watch; watch-negative vs. watch-neutral) and group-level whole-brain analyses with peak MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected thresholds, along with ROI/SVC analyses. Methods (participants, stimuli, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM) and results (behavioral, activation, PPI) are fully reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not only ROI-only, not only connectivity, empirical, includes within-task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it does NOT meet I6: the fMRI task is affect labeling, an incidental/implicit process, not an instructed emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance). Although labeling reduces amygdala activity and is discussed as incidental regulation, participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses. Satisfied inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task contrasts reported), I10 (group whole-brain maps with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (increase/decrease) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures). It reports within-task regulation contrasts (decrease > attend for negative images), uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with Talairach coordinates and cluster-thresholding, and presents results in tables/figures. Sample includes both depressed patients and matched controls with separate group analyses. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs attend) of visual sad images (IAPS and other pictures) in remitted MDD and control participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraise-sad > attend-sad), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported clusters/coordinates (tables/figures). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs cognitive reappraisal (DECREASE vs LOOK) using visual stimuli (IAPS images) and reports within-task regulation contrasts. The sample (healthy adult participants) is eligible. The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates and FWE-corrected results (including amygdala and vlPFC) and includes tables/figures/supplemental material describing whole-brain results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (sad and neutral film clips) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (Sad > Neutral). Whole-brain group-level analyses are reported with peak coordinates in standard space, and the full article includes methods, results, and discussion. The study therefore meets the review’s scope (studies of viewing visual emotional stimuli without regulation) and satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This task-based fMRI study uses visual (face) stimuli and reports the unregulated contrast (match faces vs. match shapes) and whole-brain subject-specific contrast maps, and includes healthy adult participants and behavioral measures of perceived stress and inattention. However, the fMRI task did NOT instruct an emotion regulation strategy (implicit reappraisal was inferred rather than instructed), so it fails inclusion criterion I6. Additionally, the paper does not report a group-level, voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates in standard space (no whole-brain peak coordinates/tables are provided in the main text), so it fails I10. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample), I9 (reports an unregulated viewing contrast). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed regulation), I10 (no group-level whole-brain map with coordinates). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (explicit suppression) and uses priming for implicit suppression during viewing of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and other images). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing suppression runs to baseline (e.g., EXP vs BASEEXP), Dm (subsequent memory) contrasts, group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses with tables/clusters and ROI analyses, and peak coordinates. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study using visual stimuli (IAPS) with within-task contrasts (EXP neg > neut, PRES neg > neut) and reports peak coordinates (meeting I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11), it does NOT instruct participants to implement an emotion-regulation strategy during scanning. The study selects participants on habitual use of reappraisal vs. suppression (ERQ) and examines correlations with activation, but there is no instructed regulation condition (failure to meet I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore it must be excluded because it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I6 (fMRI task with instructed emotion regulation).

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual facial stimuli and reports unregulated viewing contrasts, but it does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy during scanning (I6 not met). The paper uses an ROI-focused analysis (family-wise error within predefined ROIs) and presents ROI-derived coordinates rather than reporting a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map, so it lacks qualifying whole-brain results (I10 not met) and thus meets exclusion criterion E4. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study cannot be included.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly matches the review objective. It instructs cognitive emotion regulation (socially-induced reappraisal/distancing) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures), reports within-task contrasts (Social-Reg > Social-Look; Self-Reg > Self-Look), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that includes an instructed emotion-regulation condition: affect labeling (participants verbally label facial emotions), which functions as an incidental/instructed regulation strategy (I6). The emotional stimuli are visual (static face images) (I7). The sample includes patient (methamphetamine-dependent) and control groups with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (affect label vs affect match; and emotion viewing contrasts) (I9). Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and tables of clusters/coordinates are provided (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper reports whole-brain task activation maps (not only ROI or connectivity), includes within-group effects, and is empirical. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study must be excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met): participants performed a color-naming/ignore-the-word task rather than being instructed to reappraise, accept, distance, or otherwise regulate their emotional response. Stimuli are word stimuli (visual words), which are explicitly excluded by the review criterion (I7 not met: the review requires visual images/films; word/sentence stimuli are excluded). The study also does not report a within-task contrast of instructed emotion regulation vs viewing (I9 not met): reported contrasts are unpleasant vs neutral (emotional interference) and connectivity analyses, not regulate>view or similar. It does satisfy I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible sample), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise maps with standard-space coordinates) and I11 (coordinates/tables reported). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation in older adults that reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results. However, the regulated stimuli are personalized worry/suppression sentences (script-driven imagery / word/sentence prompts presented on the screen) rather than visual emotional stimuli (e.g., pictures, faces, film). Inclusion criterion I7 requires visual emotional stimuli and specifically excludes studies using word or sentence stimuli or purely script-driven imagery. Therefore the study fails to meet I7 and must be excluded. Included criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: worry suppression), I8 (eligible sample: elderly clinical + controls), I9 (reports within-task contrasts), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise maps), I11 (results reported in text/tables). Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to maintain versus not maintain their emotional state (an instructed emotion-control/manipulation strategy), using visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts comparing maintain > non-maintain (and emotion > neutral), conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports peak coordinates, and includes an adult sample with results at the group level. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This article meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is an empirical, task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal: “decrease negative”) during presentation of stimuli (I6). Stimuli were visual static images (negative and neutral pictures) (I7). The sample includes clinical (female adolescents with conduct disorder) and typically developing control groups reported separately (I8). Analyses report within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (decrease negative > look negative) and unregulated viewing contrasts (look negative > look neutral) (I9). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were conducted and whole-brain familywise-error-corrected results are reported (cluster-level FWE and references to peak/cluster reports), satisfying the whole-brain reporting requirement (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, within-group effects are reported). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) presented as distractors during a delayed working-memory task. The paper reports unregulated viewing contrasts (negative emotional > scrambled) and within-group as well as between-group whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (FWE-corrected), and provides full methods, results and discussion. The sample includes OCD patients and matched healthy controls with within-group effects reported. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction (e.g., reappraisal) was given, the meta-analysis objective allows inclusion of studies that view emotional stimuli without regulating; the study therefore provides an appropriate unregulated emotion contrast for inclusion. Connectivity analyses (DCM) are present but whole-brain task activations are also reported, so exclusion criterion E5 does not apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use causal attributions as an emotion-regulation strategy while viewing visual stimuli (static facial images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (internal>view, external>view, emotion-specific contrasts) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-level correction and reported coordinates/tables. Participant groups (MDD and matched healthy controls) are reported separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, imaging, preprocessing, statistics), Results (behavioral, fMRI, connectivity) and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, includes task activation maps, includes within-group effects, and the instructed task explicitly directs emotion regulation rather than mere perspective-taking). All relevant inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed emotion regulation (look, increase, decrease) using cognitive reappraisal strategies (I6). Stimuli were visual (IAPS and in-house disgusting images) (I7). The sample includes children/adolescents with ASD and TD controls (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (decrease-gross vs. look-gross; increase-gross vs. look-gross) (I9). It performed group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses and references coordinate tables/figures (Table S2, figures) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical with original fMRI task activation maps (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only), and includes within-group task effects. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because inclusion criterion I7 is NOT met: the emotional stimuli regulated are text/sentences (participant-generated autobiographical scripts and flashed negative self-belief statements), which the review’s criteria define as non-visual and thus excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation—cognitive reappraisal), I8 (sample includes clinical group with separate control group reporting), I9 (within-task contrasts reported, e.g., reappraise > react), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with standard-space coordinates), I11 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete = false).

The full text meets all inclusion requirements for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal; Suppress condition) during stimulus presentation (I6). Stimuli are visual (IAPS static images; I7). The sample is healthy adult participants (I8). The analyses report within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Suppress > Maintain, Maintain > Suppress) and parametric covariates of subjective ratings (I9). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with peak coordinates in standard space are reported (I10,I11). The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation issues). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study reports only resting-state/effective connectivity analyses without any task-evoked whole-brain activation contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample: participant groups reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation task; no cognitive reappraisal or other regulation instruction), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli—resting-state with eyes closed), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise maps reported). The article is a complete full-text report of a resting-state sDCM connectivity study and thus does not address the meta-analysis objective of task-based emotion regulation with visual stimuli. Full text appears complete for screening purposes (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (increase, decrease, maintain) during recall of previously encoded visual images (IAPS). Methods report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with coordinates/tables and contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g., decrease>maintain, increase>maintain, conjunctions, phase-specific contrasts). Sample is healthy young adults and within-task contrasts are reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text meets all required inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study that uses instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal: downregulate and upregulate) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The sample (healthy participants; genotype groups reported) is acceptable, and the paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (downregulate > look, upregulate > look, negative > neutral). Group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates and cluster thresholds in standard space, satisfying whole-brain evidence. The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation) are met.

The article reports an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use a cognitive reappraisal strategy (distancing) during presentation of visual negative and neutral pictures, satisfying I5–I7. The sample is healthy adult participants (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (RegulateNeg > WatchNeg and WatchNeg > RegulateNeg) and associated behavioral ratings (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are presented with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction (I10), and results are reported in text/figures/tables (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study includes whole-brain activation results (not ROI-only), is not a non-empirical paper, and does not report only connectivity or only between-group contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI emotion regulation with visual stimuli.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs a cognitive regulation strategy (thought suppression/self-distraction) and reports whole-brain group analyses with coordinates; however it does NOT meet the meta-analysis requirement that the regulated emotional stimuli be visual. The paradigm uses anticipatory anxiety for painful electrical stimulation with auditory cues and somatosensory (pain) stimuli, so I7 (visual stimuli) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criterion not met: I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) using visual stimuli (96 IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraise vs Maintain, Maintain vs Look) and provides peak coordinates (MNI) for activation and connectivity results, satisfying whole-brain, voxelwise reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, imaging acquisition/analysis), Results (behavioral and fMRI), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in which participants were instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal via distancing) while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS and matched photographs). The sample (ages 10.5–22.9) is eligible. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (regulation/negative > reactivity/negative) and unregulated viewing (reactivity/negative > reactivity/neutral), and conducts whole-brain group-level analyses with peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space. Reporting of coordinates and methods is detailed in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, includes task activation maps, not connectivity-only, not an empathy task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs a cognitive reappraisal (Regulate) strategy versus a control (Attend) during a sequential investment task. The stimuli are visual market displays presented on-screen and evoke emotional/regret responses related to financial decisions. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing Regulate and Attend and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with reported coordinates (MNI) and thresholding, plus tables in Supporting Information. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes an instructed emotion-regulation (reappraisal) task using visual stimuli (photographs of faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing high-control (reappraise) vs low-control (rate) and presents whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with peak coordinates (tables and figures). Sample qualifies (healthy adults). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal to increase and decrease negative affect) using visual stimuli (IAPS photographs). The sample (healthy female participants) is eligible. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (increase > look, decrease > look, look > decrease) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation). Full text is complete and includes methods, results, and discussion. Accordingly, it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (reappraisal by distancing) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS interpersonal images). Behavioral and imaging results report within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. distance > look; look > distance; negative > neutral) and interaction contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates and cluster tables in standard (MNI) space; small-volume correction was used only for the amygdala in addition to whole-brain results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs voluntary emotion regulation (detachment/distancing) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images). The sample comprises healthy adult participants and within-task contrasts (regulated vs. non-regulated; negative vs. neutral) are reported. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (with peak coordinates and FWE correction), and amygdala ROI results are also provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use emotion regulation strategies (Detachment, Reinterpretation, Distraction, Expressive Suppression) while viewing visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., ‘Regulate Negative’ > ‘Permit Negative’ and vice versa), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected results, and presents full methods, results, and discussion. Sample (healthy adults) is eligible. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly used a cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) paradigm with instructed regulation (Suppress/reappraise) and a passive Observe condition. Emotional stimuli were visual IAPS pictures. The paper reports within-task contrasts of interest (Maintain>Observe and Suppress>Maintain) and describes group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses with correction and supplementary tables for full results/coordinates. The sample includes cocaine-dependent groups and a healthy control group with group results reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion; supplementary tables are referenced but their absence does not render the main text incomplete.

This study is excluded because the emotional stimulus is auditory script-driven imagery rather than a visual stimulus, and participants were instructed to imagine the script (vividness) rather than to perform an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (e.g. reappraisal). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible sample including patient and control groups), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts such as ‘trigger vs baseline’), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates), I11 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy/cognitive reappraisal), I7 (stimuli are non-visual — audio script-driven imagery). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Maintain vs Reappraisal) using visual IAPS images, reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise vs Maintain, Maintain vs Reappraise), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates and cluster statistics. The sample (patients with panic disorder, randomized to treatment vs waiting) is acceptable per inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (study does not report only ROI/SVC or only connectivity; whole-brain analyses are present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotion (Reduce vs Maintain) while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reduce > Maintain and related effects), presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-correction (AlphaSim) and tables/figures of significant clusters, and includes an eligible sample (anxious and control groups). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; within-task effects are reported; not an empathy/perspective task without regulation). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (increase, decrease, view) while viewing visual threat-related images (IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts (increase>view, decrease>view), trial-by-trial correlations, and group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space. The methods, results, and discussion are fully present. Sample (healthy adult females) is eligible. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not connectivity-only, not ROI-only reporting).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use distraction (MEMORIZE condition) versus passive viewing to regulate emotional responses to visual stimuli (IAPS and EmoPics), with female BPD patients and control groups reported separately. The analysis includes within-task contrasts (NEGATIVE>NEUTRAL; MEMORIZE vs VIEW) and group×time×task contrasts, and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI peak coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and distraction) while presenting visual IAPS pictures to healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion induction and regulation (e.g., view NEG – view NEU; view NEG – distract; view NEG – reappraise) and provides peak coordinates in MNI space. The manuscript also states that complementary exploratory whole-brain analyses (Supplementary Table 1) are provided, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (coordinates reported in text/tables/supplement). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, non-empirical, connectivity-only analyses) apply.

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study using visual face stimuli in an appropriate sample (I5, I7, I8, I10 satisfied), it does NOT instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses (I6 not met). The task involves impression formation and social-cognitive evaluation rather than an emotion-regulation instruction (e.g., reappraise, accept, distance). While condition>baseline contrasts were modeled for use in PLS, the study does not report within-task contrasts of emotion regulation nor an explicit unregulated viewing contrast of emotional stimuli (I9 not met). The study therefore falls outside the review scope; it also meets exclusion criterion E7 (social/perspective-taking/impression-formation without instruction to amplify or dampen one’s emotional response). Excluded because E7 applies; inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I10; inclusion criteria not met: I6, I9.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (movie clips and proposal screens) in an Ultimatum Game. The paper reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., unfair > fair) and decision contrasts, with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reported peak activations (tables/figures). The sample (healthy young adult women) is acceptable. Although the study does not instruct an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal), the review objective includes studies that involve unregulated viewing; thus the study meets the review’s criteria for inclusion.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI experiment using instructed cognitive reappraisal (MAINTAIN/INCREASE/DECREASE) with visual IAPS images, includes both a patient (BPD) and healthy control group with separate reporting, presents within-task contrasts (DECREASE>MAINTAIN, INCREASE>MAINTAIN, negative>neutral), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates/tables. The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

Full text shows a task-based fMRI study that instructed emotion-regulation strategies (feel, accept, analyze) and reports whole-brain group analyses and within-task regulation contrasts. However, the emotional stimuli are autobiographical memories cued by words/phrases (script-driven imagery), not visual stimuli (no pictures, faces, scenes, or film). Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli). No exclusion criteria are met. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I7. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-based emotion regulation fMRI. It reports resting-state fMRI (seed-based rs-FC and spDCM) and behavioral ratings from an Emotion Processing Task performed outside the scanner; there is no task-based fMRI acquisition or within-task emotion-regulation instructions/contrasts (e.g., reappraise > view). Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies (reports only resting-state/seed/effective connectivity without task activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS pictures) and I8 (sample: elderly adults acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy during fMRI/task), I9 (reports within-task emotion-regulation contrasts), I10 (whole-brain task-evoked group-level activation coordinates). Full text appears complete. Consequently the study is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in which children (8–12 yrs) were instructed to use a cognitive reappraisal strategy (“MAKE-POSITIVE”) while viewing visual sad images (IAPS and child-appropriate photos). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise sad vs. view sad; view sad vs. view neutral) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with corrected thresholds) as well as ROI analyses. Core article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The full text describes a task-based fMRI experiment using instructed cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate appetitive responses to visually presented food images (static photographs). It reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Regulate Craved > Look Craved, Regulate > Look) and unregulated viewing contrasts (Look Craved > Look Not Craved, Look Craved > Look Neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-correction parameters and peak coordinates; small-ROI results for the ventral striatum are also noted but whole-brain results are primary. The sample includes adolescents (10–23 years) and results are presented in sufficient methodological and results detail (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task effects). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using instructed cognitive reappraisal with visual IAPS images in healthy adults, and it reports within-task condition comparisons. However, the fMRI analysis summarizes activation in AAL ROIs rather than reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps or peak coordinates in standard space. The paper explicitly notes use of AAL ROIs and that voxel-level/whole-brain maps are not provided. Therefore it violates exclusion E4 (only ROI-based results / no whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I10 (whole-brain evidence) and thus I11 is not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal) using visual stimuli (IAPS images and facial displays) in an appropriate adult sample and reports within-task contrasts (Look vs Decrease; Match vs Label). However, all activation effects are reported using ROI-based analyses (amygdala ROIs) and PPI connectivity analyses restricted to anatomically defined IFG masks. The paper does not present any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (analyses were mask-restricted), so it fails inclusion criterion I10 and (by implication) I11. This violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI / small-volume-corrected results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise > look contrasts) and reports within-task contrasts. Stimuli include visual faces (fearful and neutral) used during the instruction/regulation period; although top-down generation used sentences as background, the regulated stimulus during instruction is a visual face, so the study meets the visual-stimuli requirement. The sample (healthy adult women) is acceptable. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and tables/figures of activations and coordinates. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: participants were not instructed to employ an emotion regulation strategy. Instead, subjects performed a spatial cueing task and were told that faces were irrelevant (i.e., passive/ignored viewing), so no instructed regulation (reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, etc.) occurred. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli — faces), I8 (sample acceptable — older and young adults), I9 (reports within-task contrasts for unregulated viewing; emotion vs neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported), I11 (results described adequately). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E7 violations). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded solely due to failure to meet I6 (instructed emotion regulation).

This article meets all inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs explicit emotion regulation strategies including cognitive reappraisal and distraction (I6). The emotional stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). The sample includes remitted MDD patients and healthy controls with group-level results reported (I8). Analyses include within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraisal vs. view; distraction vs. view) and viewing contrasts (I9). The paper reports group-level activation peaks in standard (MNI) space (e.g., amygdala coordinates) and thresholding information, consistent with whole-brain/voxelwise reporting (I10,I11). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

The study is a task-based fMRI/ASL investigation of worry induction and instructed reappraisal in older adults and reports whole-brain voxelwise results. However, the emotional stimuli are personalized worry sentences presented as text (script-driven verbal stimuli inducing imagery), not visual emotional stimuli (e.g., images or video). This violates inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli requirement). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet I7 despite meeting other inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly investigates instructed emotion regulation (‘Enhance’ vs ‘Watch’) using visual stimuli (positive and neutral images from EmoPicS). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. PosUp > PosWatch, Up > Watch) and both ROI and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. Sample and procedures are detailed and the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

Full text is missing (API error returned) so core methods/results cannot be verified. From available metadata/title only, I cannot confirm any required inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample details), I9 (within-task contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I11 (reporting of coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria from E3–E7 can be established from the incomplete record. Because I cannot confirm the required inclusion criteria and the full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded pending full-text access. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/ not confirmed: [I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11].

This is an original, task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion-regulation manipulation (guided attentional distraction vs evaluation) with visual, static OCD-relevant and aversive images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (evaluation > distraction; OCD-relevant > neutral/aversive) and group-level, whole-brain analyses (with ROI follow-up), with results presented in figures and supplementary tables. Both patient and matched healthy control groups are reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group task effects). Full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so it is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of instructed regulation (visual stimuli) and is included.

This study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs participants to regulate negative emotion (reappraisal/distancing, suppression, distraction) while viewing visual IAPS pictures, and also includes unregulated viewing. It reports within-task contrasts comparing regulated vs. unregulated aversive stimulation (e.g., Stim_RegAv > Stim_Av and Stim_Av > Stim_RegAv), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM GLM; whole-brain FWE-corrected results and reported peak coordinates/figures/tables). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core details (participants, task, imaging, preprocessing, statistics, contrasts, coordinates) are present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based (event-related) fMRI study that explicitly instructed emotion-regulation strategies (reappraisal and expressive suppression) during an anticipation (cue) and stimulus (target) period. Visual stimuli were used (IAPS negative images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Target Reappraisal > Target Appraise, Cue Suppression > Cue Reappraisal) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and MNI coordinates in tables. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the study reports only ROI-based/small-volume-corrected task activation results with no accompanying whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level activation maps, violating exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli — IAPS images), I8 (eligible sample: healthy adults), and I9 (reports within-task contrasts/unregulated viewing contrasts such as anticipation > baseline and condition contrasts). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy — participants performed an anticipation/viewing task without regulation instructions) and I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level task-evoked statistical maps reported), and therefore I11 (reporting of whole-brain results) is also not applicable. Full text appears complete. Because E4 is met (ONLY ROI/SVC results reported), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite meeting several other inclusion items.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (volitional emotion regulation) using visual IAPS pictures. It reports within-task contrasts comparing Reappraise versus Maintain and includes whole-brain group-level voxelwise activation analyses (activation results and tables of coordinates) and supplementary tables/figures. All relevant inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplementary materials).

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain group analyses (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, it does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal or other instructed cognitive regulation); participants were instructed simply to view images while a bitter aftertaste was present. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (fMRI task with an instructed emotion-regulation strategy) is NOT met. Exclusion criteria: none of E3–E7 apply (whole-brain task activation reported; not a review; not connectivity-only; within-task effects reported; not an empathy/perspective-taking-only study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Exclusion applied because I6 not satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal) using visual stimuli (food images) in an adolescent sample, and it reports within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > imagine eating) and whole-brain analyses. However, the provided full text does not report peak activation coordinates in a standard stereotaxic space (e.g., MNI or Talairach) or tables/figures with such coordinates, which is required by inclusion criterion I10 for coordinate-based meta-analysis. Therefore I cannot confirm that I10 is satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met in the provided content. Based on the absence of reported peak coordinates in the supplied full text, the study must be excluded for failure to meet all required inclusion criteria.

The full text describes a task-based fMRI study using instructed cognitive reappraisal (and related reappraisal strategies) with visual social-affective images (IAPS and similar). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (reappraise > look-negative; look-negative > reappraise; look-negative > look-neutral) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with thresholds and cluster results) and ROI small-volume correction for the amygdala; results for patients and healthy controls are reported separately. The manuscript includes complete Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion sections. No exclusion criteria are met.

Full article reports an fMRI task with instructed cognitive reappraisal (distancing) during anticipation of visual reward cues (coins). Methods and analyses include within-task regulation contrasts (regulate > permit and interactions), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and appropriate correction, and task-based design. Sample is healthy adults. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply; full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This study should be excluded because it is not a task-based fMRI study and does not involve instructed emotion regulation of visual emotional stimuli. Inclusion IDs met: I8 (sample qualifies: older adults included), I10 (group-level whole-brain SPM analyses reported), I11 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (not fMRI — PET was used), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; tasks are working-memory/cognitive), I7 (stimuli are non-emotional visual letters/positions, not emotional images/clips), I9 (no within-task contrast related to emotion regulation or unregulated emotional viewing contrasts). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E7 apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (positive and minimizing reappraisal) using visual stimuli (IAPS images). The sample is healthy adults, analyses include within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > natural), and the paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard space. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal: “Decrease” vs. “Look”), with visual stimuli (negative and neutral images). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Regulate Negative vs. Look Negative) and also whole-brain group-level analyses (whole-brain effects and tables/figures reported, with coordinates in supplements). Sample and analyses meet inclusion requirements. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study fits the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (self-focused distancing) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures) in healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Decrease > LookNeg) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and tables/figures. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, reports whole-brain results, includes within-group task effects, not an empathy study without regulation). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study (N=51) that instructed explicit emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and suppression) while participants viewed visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to the review (View Negative > View Neutral; Reappraise > Attend Negative; Suppress > Attend Negative) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates and tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-task effects, not an empathy/perspective-taking-only design). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study that directly examines instructed emotion regulation (reappraise > look) and uninstructed viewing (look negative > look neutral) using visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > look; look negative > look neutral) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and thresholding, and presents coordinate-based results. Sample is healthy adults. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper meets several inclusion criteria (I5: task-based fMRI; I6: instructed emotion regulation with reappraisal and selective attention; I7: visual stimuli — 40 s negative film clips; I8: acceptable sample including younger and older adults; I9: reports within-task contrasts related to regulation, here as PPI contrasts such as reappraisal > passive viewing and reappraisal > selective attention). However, it violates key requirements: the article reports only seed-based functional connectivity (PPI) analyses conducted within an a priori PFC/amygdala mask and does not present a group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates in standard space (I10 not met). Therefore exclusion criteria E5 (reports ONLY seed-based/effective connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reports only ROI/small-volume-masked results with no whole-brain analysis) apply. Note: the authors state that neural activity contrasts were reported previously (Allard & Kensinger, 2014), but those whole-brain activation results are not presented in this full text. Full text appears complete for this paper. Given E4 and E5, the study must be excluded.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study using an explicit cognitive reappraisal instruction (ERT: Reappraise, Maintain, Look) with visual IAPS images. It includes a combat-exposed PTSD and control sample with results reported separately, and presents within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise > Maintain, Maintain > Look). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak MNI coordinates and tables; small-volume correction was applied for the amygdala but whole-brain maps and coordinate tables are provided. The manuscript contains complete sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus all relevant inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment instructing emotion regulation (reappraisal and distraction) using visual IAPS pictures in healthy high-risk and control groups. It provides within-task contrasts (view negative > neutral; reappraisal negative > view negative; distraction positive > view positive) from second-level random-effects analyses and gives peak coordinates in MNI space for group-level contrasts. The full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is available. Although ROI-based correction was used, group-level voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates are reported, satisfying the whole-brain coordinate reporting requirement for the meta-analysis.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI experiment that instructed participants to use an acceptance (ACCEPT) vs. natural/React (REACT) emotion-regulation strategy (meets I5,I6). Emotional visual stimuli (IAPS images) were used (meets I7), alongside thermal stimuli; the sample and exclusions are described and acceptable (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts (ACCEPT vs. REACT; Negative vs. Neutral; Hot vs. Warm) and behavioral ratings (meets I9). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported and FWE-corrected, with coordinates and conjunctions described (meets I10 and I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not non-empirical, not empathy-only). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs view) using visual stimuli (IAPS images) in adults with ADHD and matched healthy controls. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > negative view; negative view > neutral view) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with corrected cluster/voxelwise results and anatomical labels. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and reports within-group task effects. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI paper with whole-brain group-level results (meets I5, I8, I10, I11), it does NOT meet key topical inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. The fMRI task is a placebo analgesia paradigm using thermal pain stimuli and expectancy manipulation, not an instructed emotion-regulation task with visual emotional stimuli. The independent cognitive reappraisal (CRA) lab task using visual images was performed outside the scanner and not used as an in-scanner regulation instruction; there is no within-fMRI contrast of an instructed regulation condition (e.g. reappraise > look) nor any visual-emotion stimulus regulation in the scanner. Therefore inclusion criteria I6, I7 and I9 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (instructed to reappraise vs view/maintain) using visual stimuli (negative and neutral pictures). It reports within-task regulation contrasts (reappraise > view; regulation×time interactions) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI peak coordinates and cluster statistics, alongside ROI results. The sample includes BPD patients and healthy controls with separate group results and responder/nonresponder analyses. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and supplemental material is not required to verify core criteria. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs an explicit emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) and compares it with a placebo and passive viewing. Emotional stimuli are visual (disgust images/IAPS), the sample is healthy adults (female), and the paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g. Reappraisal (Disgust>Neutral), Passive Viewing (Disgust>Neutral)) and whole-brain group-level analyses (voxelwise SPM results with FWE correction). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (I5, I6). Stimuli were visual IAPS pictures (static images) (I7). The sample includes clinical groups (BD, SZ) and healthy controls with results reported separately (I8). The analyses include within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraise > attend-negative; attend-negative > attend-neutral) (I9). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were performed (3dMVM in AFNI) with cluster correction and reported cluster results (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is empirical with original fMRI data (not E3), reports whole-brain results (not only ROI; not E4), is not only connectivity/resting-state (not E5), includes within-task effects (not E6), and is not an empathy/perspective task without regulation instruction (not E7). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This paper reports a task-based fMRI study (Study 2) using an instructed cognitive reappraisal task (regulate vs experience vs observe) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It includes adults from a clinical (gambling disorder patients) and healthy control groups and provides within-task contrasts (‘regulate’ > ‘experience’, ‘experience’ > ‘observe’) and within-group activation maps. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak MNI coordinates (e.g. x = -60, y = 20, Z = 32) and cluster thresholds, meeting whole-brain reporting criteria. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Study 2 reports a task-based fMRI experiment using instructed cognitive reappraisal ("CHANGE" vs "LOOK") during presentation of visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (look negative > look neutral; decrease negative > look negative) and group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates reported (Table 5). Participant groups (DSH and depression control) are reported separately. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study using instructed affect-labeling (an implicit emotion-regulation manipulation) and an affect-matching (unregulated viewing) task with visual stimuli (photographs of emotional faces). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (affect label > gender label) and viewing (affect match > shape match). Participants include clinical (SP subgroups) and healthy control groups with group-level SPM analyses normalized to standard space; peak coordinates and whole-brain main effects are reported (supplementary table). The methods, results, and discussion are present and complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal and distraction) while presenting visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (reappraisal vs view; distraction vs view; emotion vs neutral) and describes group-level analyses. The methods state that results were thresholded and that results significant at whole-brain FWE-corrected P<0.05 are reported, and the paper describes peak activations and connectivity differences across groups; coordinates are likely provided in tables/figures/supplementary materials per the journal format. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only results; within-task effects are reported). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete for screening.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructed participants to regulate emotion (increase vs. attend vs. decrease) using cognitive reappraisal-style strategies while viewing visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts (increase>attend, decrease>attend) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected clusters and coordinates (tables/figures). Sample characteristics are acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (explicit emotion regulation) while participants view visual stimuli (negative images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraisal vs. Maintain and Reappraisal vs. Fixation), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and cluster-correction thresholds, and includes ROI analyses for the amygdala. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I5–I11) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain analyses (satisfies I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, it does NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraise/down-regulate/up-regulate/acceptance instruction); participants performed an emotion-identification/ignore-word interference task rather than an instructed regulation task. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text is complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (Reappraise vs Maintain) using visual stimuli (IAPS negative scenes; faces). The sample is healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Reappraise>Maintain) and other within-task contrasts (Surprise>Neutral, Fear>Neutral), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and peak coordinates (ROI coordinates and cluster results described). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs a cognitive reappraisal strategy (distancing) and contrasts distance vs permit conditions. Stimuli are visual (abstract cues and targets in a monetary incentive delay task) that elicit reward-related emotional responses; regulation is instructed during anticipation (expectation) and outcome periods. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Distance > Permit and related interactions), provides group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard MNI space (whole-brain/ROI analyses reported), and the full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met: this is empirical, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, and reports whole-brain voxelwise results. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which participants were explicitly instructed to apply emotion-regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal, suppression, up-regulation) while viewing visual stimuli (static high-calorie food images). The manuscript reports within-subject contrasts comparing regulation conditions (e.g., suppression vs. reappraisal, up-regulation vs. suppression) and describes a group-level, whole-brain RFX ANOVA with corrected F-map and identified fROIs in standard space. The sample (healthy adult women) is eligible. Reporting of whole-brain results and task contrasts satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. Full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present and sufficient for screening. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion-regulation (cognitive reappraisal) paradigm with visual picture stimuli. The paper reports within-task contrasts of interest (Regulate > Maintain and Maintain > Observe), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space, and provides results for both an obese patient group and healthy controls. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-visual stimuli, non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This full-text meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal variants (self-detach/self-immerse) (I6). Emotional stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). The sample includes clinical (MDD) and healthy control groups with results reported for both (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., detach > attend, immerse > attend) and within-group effects (I9). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described with reported peak coordinates in standard space (e.g., left IFG at -48,20,-4) and cluster correction (I10), and reporting in text/tables meets I11. No exclusion criteria are met: the study includes whole-brain task activation maps (not only ROIs or connectivity), includes within-group task effects, and is empirical. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs cognitive reappraisal of visual (IAPS) images and reports within-task contrasts and behavioral validation; however, the full text reports primarily ROI and seed-based (gPPI) connectivity analyses (L amygdala seed → R IFG) and does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation map (peak coordinates for a reappraise>watch type contrast) in the main article. The paper focuses on PPI connectivity and ROI-extracted beta coupling estimates, and refers to prior work and Supplement for broader results. Because the review requires at least one whole-brain task-evoked statistical map, this paper meets exclusion criterion E5 (only seed-based/ connectivity analyses reported without a whole-brain task activation map) and therefore must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (whole-brain evidence).

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed participants to perform an emotion-labeling task (affect labeling), which constitutes an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6). The emotional stimuli were visual (faces) (I7). The sample is a nonclinical adult sample reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (emotion label > gender label) and an unregulated viewing contrast (observe > fixation) (I9). Group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates are reported (I10) and results are presented in text/tables/figures (I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be included.

Exclusion reason: E4 applies — the study reports amygdala task activation using small-volume correction (ROI/SVC) and does not report a whole-brain task-evoked group activation map for the emotion contrast.
